## Campaign Overview

**Curse of Strahd** is the official D&D campaign set in Barovia, a land cursed by the ancient vampire lord Strahd von Zarovich. You've been trapped in this gothic horror realm. Your only hope: discover the source of Strahd's power and end his reign of terror—or die trying.

**Setting:** Barovia—a dark, mist-shrouded realm trapped in eternal twilight. Gothic villages, ancient forests, and crumbling castles dominate the landscape. Strahd's castle, Ravenloft, looms over everything.

**Theme:** Gothic horror with survival elements. Dark, atmospheric, and dangerous. Hope is thin; paranoia is justified. The land itself seems hostile.

**Main Conflicts:**

- Strahd von Zarovich, the vampire lord, actively hunts the party
- The land of Barovia itself is hostile and cursed
- NPCs have conflicting goals and hidden agendas
- The party must uncover Strahd's weaknesses before it's too late
- Escape from Barovia may be impossible—or may require ultimate sacrifice

frontmatter.summary: The land of Barovia resists planar travel, warps spell cosmetic manifestations, and bolsters Strahd's domain power.

entries.body:
# Alterations to Magic

The Shadowfell's grip on Barovia alters the nature of magic within its borders. While magic functions normally in most respects, the Mists isolate the valley from the rest of the multiverse and twist spell manifestations.

## Planar Restrictions

- **Barovia's Curse:** Creatures cannot leave Barovia willingly by any means, including planar travel, teleportation, or ethereal movement.
- **Planar Travel:** Spells that summon creatures or objects from other planes function normally, but creatures summoned inside Barovia cannot return to their native planes while the barrier persists.
- **Divination & Contact:** Spells that allow contact with deities, otherworldly patrons, or extraplanar beings (such as _commune_ or _contact other plane_) are intercepted or shadowed by Strahd von Zarovich, who can choose to answer or observe the communication.

## Cosmetic Alterations

The macabre atmosphere of Barovia subtly corrupts spell appearances:

- **Conjuration & Evocation:** Bright radiant energy appears pale, ghostly, or cold; fire flickers with sickly purples or deep crimsons.
- **Necromancy & Illusion:** Illusory duplicates resemble corpses, skeletons, or decaying shadows; summoned entities take on grotesque or gaunt features.
- **Find Familiar & Steeds:** Familiars and mounts take on unnerving forms (skeletal ravens, undead mastiffs, or pale skeletal cats), though their statistics remain unchanged.

## Strahd's Domain Dominance

- **Lord of the Land:** Strahd gains a **+1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls** while inside Castle Ravenloft or while the party is within 10 miles of the castle.

---

# Ra Gol'vek Campaign Rules

Ra Gol'vek is an island-rich, supernatural frontier where ancient ruins, eldritch planar rifts, and untamed oceans test mortal sanity.

---

## Setting Mechanics

### Madness Saving Throws

- **Supernatural Shock:** When characters are directly exposed to alien horrors, dimensional distortions, or unfathomable planar entities, the DM may call for a **Wisdom saving throw** (DC typically 12–18 based on severity).
- **Madness Effects:** On a failed save, the creature suffers an episode of short-term madness (rolled from the DMG Madness table, p. 259) or temporary psychic disorientation.
- **Recovery:** A short rest, restorative magic such as _lesser restoration_, or emotional grounding can end acute madness effects.

---

entries.body:
# Vyrun Campaign Rules

Vyrun's rugged mountain passes and untamed wildlands demand rigorous survival navigation, group preparedness, and endurance against brutal weather.

---

## Setting Mechanics

### Group Survival Checks

- **Wilderness Navigation:** When traversing uncharted wilderness, blizzards, or mountain passes, the party makes a **group Wisdom (Survival) check**.
- **Lowest Modifier Applies:** Rather than averaging or allowing a single ranger to guide unconditionally, the lowest Survival modifier in the travelling party sets the team's base modifier, reflecting the difficulty of moving an entire unit together through perilous terrain.
- **Success & Failure:** If at least half the party succeeds on their roll against the wilderness DC, the group stays on course. Otherwise, the party loses travel progress or encounters an environmental hazard.

### Accelerated Exhaustion

- **Harsh Exposure:** Traveling through severe blizzards, freezing alpine elevations, or torrential mountain storms without adequate shelter, fire, or cold-weather gear accelerates [[rules/conditions/exhaustion|exhaustion]].
- **Exposure Tiers:** Characters forced to march or camp without shelter in severe weather must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw every 4 hours, gaining **one level of exhaustion** on a failure in addition to normal resting requirements.

---

## Related Content

- [[campaigns/vyrun/index|Vyrun Campaign Hub]]
- [[rules|Global Rules Hub]]

entries.title: Build a Character
entries.body:
# How to Build a D&D Character

New to D&D? This guide walks you through creating your character for play.

## The Five Steps

```
Pick a RACE
    ↓
Pick a CLASS
    ↓
Pick a SUBCLASS (optional, powerful)
    ↓
Pick FEATS (customize your abilities)
    ↓
You're Ready to Play!
```

---

## Step 1: Choose a Race

Your **race** defines your ancestry and background. It gives you special abilities and traits.

**Browse races:** [[character-options/races|Races]]

Each race can have **subraces** (variants). For example, there are different types of elves. Check inside the race page for details.

**What races give you:**

- Ability score bonuses
- Special abilities (darkvision, flying, etc.)
- Cultural traits and background
- Size and appearance

---

## Step 2: Choose a Class

Your **class** is your role in the party. It determines what you're good at: fighting, casting spells, sneaking, healing, etc.

**Browse classes:** [[character-options/classes|Classes]]

Popular classes:

- **Fighter** — Master of weapons and armor
- **Wizard** — Spellcaster with arcane magic
- **Rogue** — Sneaky, dexterous, skilled
- **Cleric** — Holy spellcaster and healer
- **Barbarian** — Powerful warrior driven by rage

**What your class gives you:**

- Your main abilities and features
- Hit die (how much health you get per level)
- Spell list (if you're a spellcaster)
- Proficiencies (what you're trained in)

---

## Step 3: Choose a Subclass (Optional)

At a certain level (usually 3rd), you pick a **subclass**. This specializes your class into a specific flavor.

**Examples:**

- Fighter → [[Champion]] (master of weapons)
- Fighter → [[Crusader]] (faithful warrior)
- Wizard → [[Evocation]] (master of explosive spells)
- Wizard → [[School of Sealing]] (abjuration and binding)
- Cleric → [[Life]] (powerful healer)
- Cleric → [[Dawn Domain]] (light and dawn)

**Browse subclasses:** [[character-options/subclasses|Subclasses]]

Subclasses don't change how your class works fundamentally—they just add specialized abilities. You can play without one, but they make characters much more interesting.

---

## Step 4: Choose Feats (Optional)

**Feats** are optional bonuses that customize your character. They represent special training or talents.

You get to choose a feat at certain levels (usually 4th, 8th, 12th, etc., depending on your class).

**Example feats:**

- **[[Grappler]]** — Better at holding enemies
- **[[Courageous]]** — Stand firm against fear
- **[[Consecrated Spell]]** — Infuse spells with holy power
- **[[Celestial Blood]]** — Angelic heritage in your veins
- **Athlete** — Stronger, faster, better at physical tasks

**Browse feats:** [[character-options/feats|Feats]]

**Note:** Some feats have **prerequisites**. For example, "Great Weapon Master" requires you to have a certain fighting style. Check the prerequisite before choosing.

---

## All Your Class Options

Not just classes—your character can be customized with:

- **[[character-options/classes|Classes]]** — Your main role
- **[[character-options/subclasses|Subclasses]]** — Specialization within your role
- **[[character-options/races|Races]]** — Your ancestry and heritage
- **[[character-options/backgrounds|Backgrounds]]** — Your story before adventuring
- **[[character-options/feats|Feats]]** — Special talents and training
- **[[character-options/templates|Templates]]** — Add-ons (like becoming a werewolf, angelic being, etc.)
- **[[character-options/class-options|Character options by class]]** — Specialized choices for your class (like Warlock Invocations or Sorcerer Metamagic)

---

## Spells (If You Cast)

If your class can cast spells, look here:

**[[Spells]]** — Full spell list, sorted by class, level, and effect

Each class page (like [[Warlock]] or [[Wizard]]) lists the spells available to that class, so you don't have to search.

---

## Your Character in Campaigns

Once you've built your character, check which campaigns are available:

- **[[campaigns/ra-golvek|Ra Gol'vek]]** — Coastal intrigue, ancient magic, and supernatural threats.
- **[[Vyrun]]** — Frontier exploration, survival, and ancient mysteries.
- **[[Curse of Strahd]]** — Gothic horror in the mist-shrouded realm of Barovia.

See [[Campaigns]] for the full directory.

Pick one and jump into the adventure!

---

## Full Rules Reference

Need more details on how the game works?

**[[Rules]]** — House rules, mechanic clarifications, and campaign-specific rulings

---

## Quick Reference: Forms You'll Need

### At the Table

- Character sheet (print or digital)
- Dice for rolling
- Your spell list (if you're a caster)

### On This Site

- [[character-options/classes|Classes]] — Understanding your role
- [[character-options/subclasses|Subclasses]] — Specializing your role
- [[Spells]] — Reference while playing
- [[Items]] — Magic items and equipment
- [[Monsters]] — What enemies look like

---

## Still Confused?

Each page has more details. Click the links above to dive deeper. And remember: **D&D is collaborative**. Talk to your Dungeon Master if you're unsure about anything.

Have fun!

---

frontmatter.title: Acolyte
frontmatter.summary: Skills: Insight, Religion

entries.body:
**Skill proficiencies:** Insight, Religion  
**Languages:** 2 of your choice  
**Equipment:** Clothes, common, Pouch

> [!info]- Feature: Shelter of the Faithful
> As an acolyte, you command the respect of those who share your faith, and you can perform the religious ceremonies of your deity. You and your adventuring companions can expect to receive free healing and care at a temple, shrine, or other established presence of your faith, though you must provide any material components needed for spells. Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle.
>
> You might also have ties to a specific temple dedicated to your chosen deity or pantheon, and you have a residence there. This could be the temple where you used to serve, if you remain on good terms with it, or a temple where you have found a new home. While near your temple, you can call upon the priests for assistance, provided the assistance you ask for is not hazardous and you remain in good standing with your temple.

## Personality traits

1. I idolize a particular hero of my faith, and constantly refer to that person's deeds and example.
2. I can find common ground between the fiercest enemies, empathizing with them and always working toward peace.
3. I see omens in every event and action. The gods try to speak to us, we just need to listen.
4. Nothing can shake my optimistic attitude.
5. I quote (or misquote) sacred texts and proverbs in almost every situation.
6. I am tolerant (or intolerant) of other faiths and respect (or condemn) the worship of other gods.
7. I've enjoyed fine food, drink, and high society among my temple's elite. Rough living grates on me.
8. I've spent so long in the temple that I have little practical experience dealing with people in the outside world.

## Ideals

1. Tradition. The ancient traditions of worship and sacrifice must be preserved and upheld.
2. Charity. I always try to help those in need, no matter what the personal cost.
3. Change. We must help bring about the changes the gods are constantly working in the world.
4. Power. I hope to one day rise to the top of my faith's religious hierarchy.
5. Faith. I trust that my deity will guide my actions. I have faith that if I work hard, things will go well.
6. Aspiration. I seek to prove myself worthy of my god's favor by matching my actions against his or her teachings.

## Bonds

1. I would die to recover an ancient relic of my faith that was lost long ago.
2. I will someday get revenge on the corrupt temple hierarchy who branded me a heretic.
3. I owe my life to the priest who took me in when my parents died.
4. Everything I do is for the common people.
5. I will do anything to protect the temple where I served.
6. I seek to preserve a sacred text that my enemies consider heretical and seek to destroy.

## Flaws

1. I judge others harshly, and myself even more severely.
2. I put too much trust in those who wield power within my temple's hierarchy.
3. My piety sometimes leads me to blindly trust those that profess faith in my god.
4. I am inflexible in my thinking.
5. I am suspicious of strangers and expect the worst of them.
6. Once I pick a goal, I become obsessed with it to the detriment of everything else in my life.

entries.summary: Skills: Insight, Persuasion

frontmatter.title: Benefactor
frontmatter.summary: Skills: Insight, Persuasion

entries.body:
Benefactors are those who work for the well-being of the people around them. They spend their time helping build houses, cook, or hand out supplies. They are generally beloved by all, because not everyone dedicates their life to the well-being of others.

A benefactor can be someone who helps people in their daily comings or goings, can come from a wealthy family and decide to use their treasures to help people or be someone who provides supplies to a wartorn village against all odds. In any case, as a benefactor, you've dedicated your life to making the world a better place; step by step and day by day.

**Skill proficiencies:** Insight, Persuasion  
**Languages:** Two of your choice  
**Equipment:** A small knife, a scroll that reads "Do you need help?" in Common, a set of common clothes, and a belt pouch containing 20 gp

> [!info]- Feature: Name of Kindness
> Your good deeds earned you a reputation in the settlements nearby. Those you introduce yourself to tend to think you have a good heart, which makes them eager to assist you in your adventures. For instance, they may provide you with food, shelter or information.

## Suggested characteristics

Benefactors always have people's best interests at heart. They thus don't like wasting their time with things that don't seem to be helping anyone. They also tend to be sociable, as their job mainly focuses on people. They listen to those who need help and try to comfort them. Overall, most benefactors are cheerful people with hearts full of hope.

| d8  | Personality trait                                                                      |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | I like to play harmless pranks on others.                                              |
| 2   | When I am with people, I try to be serious.                                            |
| 3   | I like being around children. They remind me of the lighter and brighter side of life. |
| 4   | I'm always intrigued by real-life stories.                                             |
| 5   | I speak to everyone like they're my friends.                                           |
| 6   | I don't like stingy folk who don't share their belongings.                             |
| 7   | I like to collect mementos from the settlements I help.                                |
| 8   | I am committed to my deity with my life.                                               |

| d6  | Ideal                                                                                                                              |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Foundation. I will create an organization to help people all across the land. (Good)                                               |
| 2   | Humble. Those I've saved may see me as their savior, thinking they owe me their lives. Yet I was only doing what was right. (Good) |
| 3   | Kindness. No matter what, I will help everyone. There's nothing that could change my mind. (Good)                                  |
| 4   | Justice. All those who hurt the innocent will pay for their crimes in accordance with the law. (Lawful Good)                       |
| 5   | Power. Once I become powerful enough, I can stop all violence. (Any)                                                               |
| 6   | Equality. None should suffer. (Any)                                                                                                |

| d6  | Bond                                                                                                                    |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | While I was trying to help someone, I accidentally got them killed. I now can't shake the fear of losing someone again. |
| 2   | I carry an item that reminds me of the first time I risked my life to save people.                                      |
| 3   | I lost my family in a horrible event. From that day forward, I've dedicated myself to saving others.                    |
| 4   | When I am under stress, I start humming a melody, the lullaby my mother sang to me when I was a child.                  |
| 5   | Since I always side with innocents, I'm not always welcome everywhere.                                                  |
| 6   | I provide supplies to a small village from time to time. I must make sure they are doing okay.                          |

| d6  | Flaw                                                                  |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | I've had to work with shady folk to help others.                      |
| 2   | Seeing innocent people getting hurt blinds me with rage.              |
| 3   | Secretly, I enjoy killing evildoers. It's what they deserve.          |
| 4   | When someone flirts with me, I am charmed by them almost immediately. |
| 5   | I tend to flee from fights when I feel desperate.                     |
| 6   | I can't stand gore.                                                   |

_From Corpus Angelus._
