## Spellcasting

_2nd-level Tamer feature_

**Tamer spells:** The catalogue below contains the supplied Appendix B spell list. Existing archive spells retain their original provenance; Appendix B records without full definitions remain marked incomplete for transcription review.

![[tamer-spells.base]]

Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your Tamer spellcasting ability.

- **Spell save DC** = 8 + proficiency bonus + spellcasting ability modifier
- **Spell attack modifier** = proficiency bonus + spellcasting ability modifier

A companion's vessel can serve as your spellcasting focus.

## Bolster

_2nd-level Tamer feature_

While your companion is within 100 feet and you hold its vessel, expend a spell slot as an action to restore hit points equal to your spellcasting ability modifier, minimum 1, plus 2d4 per level of the slot.

## Psychic Bond

_2nd-level Tamer feature_

While your companion is within 100 feet, communicate telepathically. As an action, see and hear through its senses until the start of your next turn; you are deaf and blind to your own senses during that time.

While your companion is summoned, within 100 feet, and you hold its vessel, its known spells are added to your known spells. A spell with a range of self or touch can target your companion.

## Pocket Family

_3rd-level Tamer feature_

You can bond with two companions at 3rd level, three at 7th, four at 11th, five at 15th, and six at 19th. Your maximum companion size becomes Medium at 5th level, Large at 11th, and Huge at 17th level.

## Training Paradigm

_3rd-level Tamer feature_

Choose one of the following paradigms:

- [[character-options/subclasses/Tamer|Tamer Training Paradigms]]

Your paradigm grants features at 3rd, 7th, 10th, and 14th level. Its 7th-level feature improves at 18th level.

## Ability Score Improvement

_4th-level Tamer feature_

At 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat for which you qualify.

## Multiattack

_5th-level Tamer feature_

When you command your companion, you can command it to use Multiattack if it has that action.

## Malleable Presence

_5th-level Tamer feature_

Command your companion to impose either Aggressive or Cautious behavior on a creature you can see. The target makes Wisdom saving throws against your spell save DC at the start of its turns for one minute.

**Aggressive:** Disadvantage on attacks against creatures other than your companion.  
**Cautious:** Disadvantage on attacks against your companion if another hostile creature is within 5 feet of the attacker.

Once used, this feature returns after a short or long rest.

## Alpha Strike

_6th-level Tamer feature_

As part of summoning a companion, command it to take an action. Uses equal your spellcasting ability modifier, minimum once, regained on a long rest.

## Wilful Blows

_6th-level Tamer feature_

Your companions' attacks count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

## Switcheroo

_13th-level Tamer feature_

While you and a companion are within 100 feet, use a bonus action or reaction to switch places. Uses equal your spellcasting ability modifier, minimum once, regained on a long rest.

## Magnificent Presence

_17th-level Tamer feature_

Command a companion to adopt Provoking Poise or Shrinking Violet for one minute. Once used, this feature returns after a long rest.

## Summon the Horde

_20th-level Tamer feature

As an action, summon additional companions for one minute, up to three simultaneously from this feature. Command all companions with one action. When the minute ends, all but one return to their vessels and you cannot move or act until the end of your next turn.

Once used, this feature returns after a long rest.

entries.body:
# Thanatomancer

Thanatomancers are spellcasters bound to the Mortis Veil, the shroud separating life from death. They wield necrotic energy to unravel life, manipulate entropy, and sustain themselves through destruction.

## Character creation

### Quick build

Make Intelligence your highest ability score, followed by Constitution. Choose the sage or hermit background. Choose the _soul scythe_, _ray of frost_, and _Malcorith's grim gaze_ cantrips, along with the 1st-level spells _false life_ and _inflict wounds_.

### Hit points

**Hit dice:** 1d8 per thanatomancer level  
**Hit points at 1st level:** 8 + your Constitution modifier  
**Hit points at higher levels:** 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier per thanatomancer level after 1st

### Proficiencies

**Armor:** Light armor  
**Weapons:** Simple weapons  
**Tools:** None  
**Saving throws:** Constitution, Intelligence  
**Skills:** Choose three from Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Religion, and Stealth

### Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

- (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) any simple weapon
- (a) a scholar's pack or (b) an explorer's pack
- An arcane focus

## Spellcasting

_1st-level Thanatomancer feature_

The thanatomancer spell list consists of necromancy, enchantment, and divination spells from the cleric, druid, and wizard spell lists.

**Browse available Thanatomancer spells by level:**

![[thanatomancer-spells.base]]

### Cantrips

At 1st level, you know three cantrips of your choice from the thanatomancer spell list. You learn additional cantrips as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Thanatomancer table.

### Spell slots

The Thanatomancer table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your thanatomancer spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

### Spells known of 1st level and higher

You know two 1st-level spells of your choice from the thanatomancer spell list. The Spells Known column of the Thanatomancer table shows when you learn more spells. Each spell you choose must be of a level for which you have spell slots. Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one thanatomancer spell you know with another spell of your choice from the thanatomancer spell list. The new spell must be a necromancy, enchantment, or divination spell from the cleric, druid, or wizard spell lists, and it must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

### Spellcasting ability

Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your thanatomancer spells. You use your Intelligence whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability.

**Spell save DC** = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier  
**Spell attack modifier** = your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

### Ritual casting

You can cast any thanatomancer spell you know as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag.

### Spellcasting focus

You can use an arcane focus as a spellcasting focus for your thanatomancer spells.

## Class features

> [!info]- Veil Techniques (level 1)
> You can manipulate the Mortis Veil through Veil Techniques, which are fueled by mortis points.
>
> - You can have a maximum of 2 mortis points. Starting at 3rd level, your maximum increases by 1 for each thanatomancer level you gain.
> - You expend mortis points to activate Veil Techniques. You regain all expended mortis points when you finish a long rest.
> - You learn two Veil Techniques of your choice at 1st level and one additional technique at 3rd, 7th, 11th, and 15th level.
> - When you finish a long rest, you can replace one technique you know with a different available technique.
> - When you use a technique, expend the mortis points specified in its description. You can use only one Veil Technique per turn, unless otherwise stated. If a technique requires a saving throw, it uses your spell save DC.
>
> Starting at 7th level, when you activate a Veil Technique, you can expend 1 additional mortis point to gain its 7th-level enhancement. Starting at 13th level, you can expend 2 additional mortis points to gain its 13th-level enhancement. You can pay for either or both enhancements.
>
> The available techniques appear below.

> [!info]- Deathlike Reflexes (level 2)
> When a creature you can see targets you with an attack, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll. You must decide before the result is known. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum once), regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

> [!info]- Thanatology Path (level 3)
> You choose a Thanatology Path, which grants features at 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 18th level: the [[Path of the Fleshweaver]], [[Path of the Graveguard]], or [[Path of the Reaper]].

> [!info]- Ability Score Improvement (levels 4, 8, 12, 16, 19)
> When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score by 2, or increase two ability scores by 1. You can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. If your campaign uses the optional feat rules, you can take a feat instead.

> [!info]- Soul Reservoir (level 5)
> When a hostile creature within 30 feet of you is killed, you gain 1 mortis point unless you are already at your maximum. If you are at your maximum, choose one of the following effects until the end of your next turn instead:
>
> - You gain temporary hit points equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1).
> - You have advantage on your next attack roll.
>
> You can regain mortis points this way a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1). After doing so, you can't regain mortis points with this feature again until you finish a short or long rest.
>
> Immediately after you finish a short rest, you can expend a spell slot of a level equal to or lower than your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1) to regain mortis points equal to the level of the spell slot expended.

> [!info]- Gravebound Form (level 9)
> You gain resistance to necrotic and poison damage, immunity to disease, and advantage on death saving throws.

> [!info]- Veil Dominion (level 14)
> When you cast a spell that deals necrotic damage, you ignore resistance to necrotic damage and treat immunity to necrotic damage as resistance.

> [!info]- Avatar of Thanatos (level 20)
> As a bonus action, you assume the form of Thanatos for 1 minute. While in this form, you are immune to necrotic and poison damage, and your necromancy spells deal maximum damage instead of rolling. Each creature of your choice that starts its turn within 30 feet of you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or take necrotic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1) + your proficiency bonus. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

## Veil Technique options

### Corrupting Essence

When you hit a creature with a weapon attack or deal damage with a spell attack that targets only one creature, you can expend 1 mortis point to deal extra necrotic damage to it equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1). The next time you deal damage to that creature before the end of your next turn, it takes necrotic damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

- **7th level:** Expend 1 additional mortis point to gain advantage on the next attack roll you make against the branded creature before the end of your next turn.
- **13th level:** Expend 2 additional mortis points. Until the start of your next turn, the creature has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes.

### Entropic Decay

When you hit a creature with a weapon attack or deal damage with a spell that targets only one creature, you can expend 2 mortis points to curse it with lingering entropy. The target can't regain hit points until the start of your next turn.

- **7th level:** Expend 1 additional mortis point. Until the start of your next turn, the target takes extra necrotic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1) for every 5 feet it moves.
- **13th level:** Expend 2 additional mortis points. For the next minute, at the start of each of its turns, the target suffers a cumulative −1 penalty (maximum −3) to attack and damage rolls. At the end of each of its turns, it can make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, ending the effect on itself on a success.

### Gravebind

When you deal damage to a creature with a weapon attack or deal necrotic damage with a spell that targets only one creature, you can expend 2 mortis points. The creature takes necrotic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1) and must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be restrained until the end of its next turn.

- **7th level:** If the creature fails its save, expend 1 additional mortis point. When its restrained condition ends, it takes extra necrotic damage equal to your thanatomancer level.
- **13th level:** Expend 2 additional mortis points to prevent the creature from teleporting or entering the Ethereal Plane until the end of its next turn.

### Pierce the Veil

As an action, expend 1 mortis point to attune your senses to the Mortis Veil for 1 minute. You sense the presence and direction, but not exact location, of Undead creatures and corpses that died within the past 24 hours within 30 feet. You also have advantage on Wisdom (Medicine and Perception) and Intelligence (Investigation and Religion) checks related to death, undeath, or necromancy.

- **7th level:** Expend 1 additional mortis point. For the duration, you gain tremorsense out to 10 feet and darkvision out to 60 feet (or extend your existing darkvision by 30 feet); magical darkness doesn't impede your darkvision.
- **13th level:** Expend 2 additional mortis points. Until the end of your next turn, you can see into the Ethereal Plane and detect invisible creatures within 30 feet as faint blurs.

### Reaper's Shroud

As a reaction when you fail a saving throw against being charmed, frightened, paralyzed, possessed, or stunned, expend 1 mortis point to immediately reroll the saving throw. You must use the new result.

- **7th level:** Expend 1 additional mortis point to extend the shroud until the end of your next turn. While shrouded, you have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, frightened, paralyzed, possessed, or stunned.
- **13th level:** Expend 2 additional mortis points to shroud one ally within 30 feet when you activate this technique. That ally has advantage on saving throws against being charmed, frightened, paralyzed, possessed, or stunned until the end of their next turn.

### Sapping Strike

When you hit a creature with a weapon attack or deal damage with a spell that targets only one creature, expend 1 mortis point to sap its momentum. Until the end of its next turn, the target's speed is halved and it can't take reactions.

- **7th level:** Expend 1 additional mortis point to give the target disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws until the end of its next turn.
- **13th level:** Expend 2 additional mortis points. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or be hindered until the end of its next turn. While hindered, it can take either an action or a bonus action on its turn, not both.

### Withering Grasp

When you hit a creature with a weapon attack or deal damage with a spell attack that targets only one creature, expend 1 mortis point to wither its vitality. The target has disadvantage on the next Strength or Constitution saving throw it makes before the end of your next turn.

- **7th level:** Expend 1 additional mortis point to give the target disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of your next turn.
- **13th level:** Expend 2 additional mortis points to unmake the target's resistances. The creature loses any resistance to necrotic damage until the end of your next turn. If it is immune to necrotic damage, it instead has resistance to necrotic damage for the same duration.

### Wraith's Reflex

When an attacker you can see hits you with a melee attack, use your reaction and expend 1 mortis point to phase out of existence and move up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see without provoking opportunity attacks.

- **7th level:** Expend 1 additional mortis point to become intangible until the end of your next turn. You can move through creatures as if they were difficult terrain. If you end your turn inside a creature, you are shunted to the last unoccupied space you left and take 1d10 force damage for every 5 feet moved.
- **13th level:** Expend 2 additional mortis points to become incorporeal until the start of your next turn. You gain resistance to all damage except force and radiant, and immunity to the grappled and restrained conditions.

## Thanatology Paths

- [[Path of the Fleshweaver]]
- [[Path of the Graveguard]]
- [[Path of the Reaper]]

_From Erevan's Guide to Death & Beyond._

entries.body:
# The Warlock

A striking tiefling with an auburn complexion and dark horns stands in a ritual circle beneath the full moon. As he chants in a forgotten tongue, the moon is swallowed by darkness. A voice beyond the stars offers power if he works toward its goals. He agrees, and the moonlight returns as eldritch power fills him.

A massive goliath carves an eldritch idol from the bones of a guardian beast. Steeped in the jungle's magic, its bones become a vessel for the power he discovered in its temple.

A dark warrior faces cultists of a rival demon lord. He conjures a clear blue-ice axe and moves with impossible speed, fueled by the frigid magic of a powerful fiend. When his foes fall, the axe melts away.

These occult mages are Warlocks. Through dark secrets, sinister magic, and bargains with powerful entities, they gain power from many traditions.

## Lure of Secrets

Driven by an irresistible thirst for knowledge, warlocks pursue lost lore and power through any shortcut available. Small idols, totems, holy symbols, and other occult trinkets hold fragments of secret magic, often drawn from several traditions at once. No relic is too sacred, no forbidden text too dangerous, and no tomb too risky when it may contain knowledge or power.

## Dire Bargains

Warlocks seek power for many reasons: wealth, glory, protection, service, or revenge. Their pursuit eventually brings them to powerful otherworldly beings. Some willingly make a bargain, some trick an entity into lending power, and others secretly draw magic from such beings. However it begins, every warlock's power is bound to a dire bargain.

## Creating Your Warlock

Consider why your character pursues knowledge and power. Are they driven to uncover lost secrets? Has an entity enlisted them as its agent? Do they seek power to serve others? Also consider how their spells and invocations manifest: do they draw from several occult traditions, or resemble the magic of a more traditional mage?

## Class Features

### Hit Points

- **Hit Dice:** 1d8 per warlock level
- **Hit Points at 1st Level:** 8 + your Constitution modifier
- **Hit Points at Higher Levels:** 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier per warlock level after 1st

### Proficiencies

- **Armor:** Light armor
- **Weapons:** Simple weapons
- **Tools:** None
- **Saving Throws:** Wisdom, Intelligence
- **Skills:** Choose two from Arcana, Deception, History, Intimidation, Investigation, Nature, and Religion

### Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

- (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) any simple weapon
- (a) a component pouch or (b) an arcane focus
- (a) a scholar's pack or (b) a dungeoneer's pack
- Leather armor, any simple weapon, and two daggers

### Quick Build

Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your highest ability score, followed by Constitution. Choose the Charlatan background. For starting invocations, choose Eyes of the Rune Keeper and Mask of Many Faces.

### Multiclassing and the Warlock

If your group uses multiclassing, you need a score of 13 in Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma to take a Warlock level or a level in another class while you are a warlock. This must be your Pact Spellcasting Ability. If Warlock is not your initial class, you gain proficiency with light armor and simple weapons.

## Eldritch Invocations

At 1st level, you bind two invocations to Trinkets. A lost or destroyed Trinket reforms on your person at the end of your next short or long rest. The Invocations Known column shows when you learn additional invocations. You can learn an invocation when you meet its prerequisites. When you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one invocation you know with another for which you qualify.

Browse the complete [[character-options/class-options/eldritch-invocations/index|Eldritch Invocations catalogue]].

### Eldritch Spellcasting

Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your Pact Ability. Use it whenever an invocation or spell refers to your Spellcasting Ability, sets a saving throw DC, or requires a spell attack roll.

- **Spell save DC:** 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Pact modifier
- **Spell attack modifier:** your Proficiency Bonus + your Pact modifier

### Eldritch Blast

While holding a Trinket containing an invocation, use your action to make a ranged spell attack against one creature you can see within 120 feet. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 + your Pact modifier Force damage.

### Otherworldly Patron

At 2nd level, choose an Otherworldly Patron. Your Patron grants features at 2nd, 6th, 10th, and 14th levels. If a Patron feature forces a saving throw, it uses your Pact save DC.

### Patron Magic

Each Patron grants spells at the Warlock levels listed in its description. These spells count as Warlock spells for you but do not count against your Spells Known.

### Pact Magic

At 2nd level, you learn two cantrips from the Warlock spell list. You learn another cantrip at 4th and 10th levels. The Warlock table shows your spell slots and their level. All your slots are the same level, and you regain expended slots after a short or long rest.

At 2nd level, you know three 1st-level Warlock spells. The Spells Known column shows when you learn more. A spell must be no higher than your Slot Level. When you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one known Warlock spell with another Warlock spell of a level you can cast.

Spells learned from an invocation count as Warlock spells but do not count against your Spells Known. You can use an invocation-bearing Trinket or an arcane focus as a Spellcasting Focus.

Browse available Warlock spells by level:

![[warlock-spells.base]]

## Pact Focus

At 3rd level, choose one of the [[character-options/class-options/pact-foci/index|Pact Foci]]. Each option's record gives its rules.

### Eldritch Familiars

When you choose Eldritch Familiar, conjure one of the [[character-options/class-options/familiars/index|Eldritch Familiar forms]]. Each record contains the applicable stat block.

### Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. You cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

### Empowered Blast

At 5th level, Eldritch Blast creates two beams. It creates three beams at 11th level and four at 17th level. You can direct each beam at the same target or different targets, making a separate spell attack roll for each.

### Elder Arcanum

At 11th level, choose an Elder Arcanum for which you meet the prerequisites. You learn another at 13th, 15th, and 17th level. Once learned, an Arcanum cannot be replaced.

Browse the [[character-options/class-options/elder-arcana/index|Elder Arcanum catalogue]].

### Seat at the Table

At 20th level, choose a second Otherworldly Patron. You gain that Patron's 2nd-level features and all of its Patron Spells.

Whenever you finish a long rest, you may replace this secondary Patron with another Otherworldly Patron available to Warlocks.

## Hit points

**Hit dice:** 1d6 per wizard level  
**Hit points at 1st level:** 6 + your Constitution modifier  
**Hit points at higher levels:** 1d6 (or 4) + your Constitution modifier per wizard level after 1st

## Proficiencies

**Armor, weapons, and tools:** Daggers, Darts, Slings, Quarterstaffs, Crossbows, light  
**Saving throws:** INT, WIS  
**Skills:** Choose two from Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, and Religion

## Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

- (a) a quarterstaff or (b) a dagger
- (a) a component pouch or (b) an arcane focus
- (a) a scholar’s pack or (b) an explorer’s pack
- Spellbook

## Spellcasting

**Browse available Wizard spells by level:**

![[wizard-spells.base]]

---

> [!info]- Cantrips
> At 1st level, you know three cantrips of your choice from the wizard spell list. You learn additional wizard cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Wizard table.

> [!info]- Spellbook
> At 1st level, you have a spellbook containing six 1st- level wizard spells of your choice. Your spellbook is the repository of the wizard spells you know, except your cantrips, which are fixed in your mind.

> [!info]- Preparing and Casting Spells
> The Wizard table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.
>
> You prepare the list of wizard spells that are available for you to cast. To do so, choose a number of wizard spells from your spellbook equal to your Intelligence modifier + your wizard level (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
>
> For example, if you're a 3rd-level wizard, you have four 1st-level and two 2nd-level spell slots. With an Intelligence of 16, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of 1st or 2nd level, in any combination, chosen from your spellbook. If you prepare the 1st-level spell magic missile, you can cast it using a 1st-level or a 2nd-level slot. Casting the spell doesn't remove it from your list of prepared spells.
>
> You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of wizard spells requires time spent studying your spellbook and memorizing the incantations and gestures you must make to cast the spell: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.

> [!info]- Spellcasting Ability
> Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your wizard spells, since you learn your spells through dedicated study and memorization. You use your Intelligence whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a wizard spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
>
> Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier.
>
> Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier.

> [!info]- Ritual Casting
> You can cast a wizard spell as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag and you have the spell in your spellbook. You don't need to have the spell prepared.

> [!info]- Spellcasting Focus
> You can use an arcane focus as a spellcasting focus for your wizard spells.

## Multiclassing

**Prerequisites:** INT 13

## Class features

> [!info]- Arcane Recovery (level 1)
> You have learned to regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. Once per day when you finish a short rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your wizard level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher.
>
> For example, if you're a 4th-level wizard, you can recover up to two levels worth of spell slots. You can recover either a 2nd-level spell slot or two 1st-level spell slots.

> [!info]- Spellcasting: Wizard (level 1)
> As a student of arcane magic, you have a spellbook containing spells that show the first glimmerings of your true power.

> [!info]- Arcane Tradition (level 2)
> When you reach 2nd level, you choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic through one of eight schools, such as Evocation.
>
> Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

> [!info]- Ability Score Improvement (levels 4, 8, 12, 16, 19)
> When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

> [!info]- Arcane Tradition feature (levels 6, 10, 14)
> When you reach 2nd level, you choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic through one of eight schools, such as Evocation.
>
> Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

> [!info]- Spell Mastery (level 18)
> At 18th level, you have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a 1st-level wizard spell and a 2nd-level wizard spell that are in your spellbook. You can cast those spells at their lowest level without expending a spell slot when you have them prepared. If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.
>
> By spending 8 hours in study, you can exchange one or both of the spells you chose for different spells of the same levels.

> [!info]- Signature Spell (level 20)
> When you reach 20th level, you gain mastery over two powerful spells and can cast them with little effort. Choose two 3rd-level wizard spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, they don't count against the number of spells you have prepared, and you can cast each of them once at 3rd level without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
>
> If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.

## Updated Defensive Duelist Feat

**Prerequisite:** Dexterity of 13 or higher

When a creature you can see hits you with a melee attack while you are wielding a finesse or light melee weapon you are proficient with, you can use your reaction to add your Dexterity modifier to your Armor Class against that attack.

entries.title: Feats
entries.body:
# Feats

**Feats** are special abilities you can take instead of ability score increases.

Gain at levels 4, 8, 12, 16, and 19 (unless your class says otherwise). The table below lists feats in this archive, including Fighter feats, Monk feats, and SRD [[Grappler]].

---

## What is a feat?

A feat gives you a special power, skill boost, resistance, or talent. Some have prerequisites.

---

## How feats work

**Every 4 levels,** you can either:

- Increase an **ability score** (for example +2 STR, or +1 to two scores)
- Take a **feat** instead

---

**Step 1:** Reach a feat-gaining level (4, 8, 12, 16, 19)  
**Step 2:** Decide: ability score increase or feat?

**Prerequisite:** Intimidation proficiency

You use fear and intimidation to rally those who follow you into battle.

**Ability Score Increase.** Increase your Strength, Constitution, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

entries.title: Oathbound
entries.summary: Prerequisite: You must have an oath

frontmatter.title: Oathbound
frontmatter.summary: Prerequisite: You must have an oath

entries.body:
**Prerequisite:** You must have an oath

Oaths have a special meaning and hold power within universal forces. When someone takes an oath, some of these forces start to watch the oathbound. These forces can be fiends trying to make the oathbound deviate from the righteous path, or angels that wish to help, reward, or punish them according to their actions.

You made an oath, whether you know the facts above or not; either to yourself, to another person, or to a celestial. Now, the oath is one of the most important things in your life and you are bound to it.

Until you fulfill your oath, you have a +2 bonus on ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws that are directly related to your oath. Whether the roll is directly related or not is determined by the GM.

If you break your oath, you take a -2 penalty to all ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws until you atone for your mistake or are targeted by a wish spell. To atone, you must either spend 40 days in seclusion without talking and with no one to talk to, thinking about your sins and wrongdoings, or you must be blessed by the bless spell cast by a good-aligned spellcaster of 17th level or higher.

When you fulfill your oath, you are no longer oathbound. You do, however, receive the blessing of the divine; granting you a +2 bonus to all ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws.

GMs may choose to give this feat to a character when it takes a serious oath, even if the character shouldn't be able to gain a new feat under normal circumstances.

Keep in mind, you can only receive blessing from the divine once in this way. So, for instance, you do not gain the bonuses again if you take a second oath and then fulfill it.

_From Corpus Angelus._

frontmatter.summary: Teaches Savage Exploits and provides Exploit Dice

entries.body:
# Savage Training

You can draw upon the anger within your soul to perform Savage Exploits.

**Savage Exploits Known.** Learn two 1st-degree Savage Exploits from the [[character-options/classes/Barbarian|Alternate Barbarian]] list. If an Exploit requires a save DC, it equals 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice).

**Retraining Exploits.** Whenever you gain a level, you can replace one Savage Exploit learned through this feat with another 1st-degree Savage Exploit of your choice.

**Exploit Dice.** You gain two d4 Exploit Dice to fuel these Exploits, expended when used and regained after a short or long rest. If you already have Exploit Dice when you gain this feat, you instead gain one Exploit Die equal to your others.

entries.summary: Alternate Fighter feat

frontmatter.summary: Alternate Fighter feat

entries.body:
# Signature Technique

**Prerequisites:** At least one Martial Exploit Known

You have practiced a single technique to the point of mastery. Choose a 1st-degree Exploit you know from those available to the Alternate Fighter that does not restore hit points.

In combat, you can use this Exploit once per round without expending an Exploit Die, rolling a d4 for the Exploit Die. You regain this feature at the start of each of your turns.

entries.title: Starcaster
entries.summary: Prerequisite: Spellcasting feature

frontmatter.title: Starcaster
frontmatter.summary: Prerequisite: Spellcasting feature

entries.body:
**Prerequisite:** Spellcasting feature

You are able to imbue yourself with the arcane powers of the stars. You gain the following benefits:

- Increase your Intelligence score by 1, up to a maximum of 20.
- As an action, you can imbue any spell with the power of the stars for 1 minute. When you do so, the damage-dealing spells you cast within the duration deal radiant damage instead of their normal damage type.
- At night, you are guided by the stars. Thus, you can't be lost during the night.

_From Corpus Angelus._

When you were infused with life during your creation, you were blessed three times instead of once, and it now shows. You gain the following benefits:

- Increase your Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
- When your blood is spilled onto soil, small plants native to your location start to grow at the spot and blossom.
- When you take damage, you regain 1 hit point at the start of each of your turns until the total of the hit points you regained is equal to the damage you took or until you take any more damage.

When you choose this feat, angels start to watch over you. You gain the following benefits:

- Increase one ability score of your choice by 1, to a maximum of 20.
- Once per day, the first attack that drops you to 0 hit points misses you instead. Since you have no control over the angels watching you, the GM decides if you can benefit from this feature.

# Weapon Adept

## Updated Weapon Master Feat

You have spent many hours honing your skills with the deadly armaments of war. You gain the benefits listed below:

Ability Score Increase. Increase either your Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution score by 1, up to a maximum of 20.

Weapon Training. You gain proficiency with all simple and martial weapons.

frontmatter.title: Weapon Master
frontmatter.summary: Alternate Fighter feat

entries.body:
# Weapon Master

Proficiency with all simple and martial weapons You wield weapons with a deadly efficiency that is impressive even to most trained warriors. Choose a number of simple or martial weapons equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Whenever you make an attack with those weapons you gain a +1 bonus to both the attack and damage roll.

As your Proficiency Bonus increases, you choose additional weapons to gain this benefit.

Wings made of your innate light sprout from your back. You gain the following benefits:

- As a bonus action, you can make your wings sprout or disappear. While you have your wings spread, you have a flying speed of 30 feet.
- Your wings shed bright, magical light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. Magical darkness doesn't impede your wings' magical light.

You can drag Grappled creatures up to your full speed. In place of an attack, you can make another Grapple check against a target you are Grappling. On a success, the target is Restrained for the duration of that Grapple.

# Fighting Styles

**Martial techniques available through features from multiple classes and other character options.**

These styles offer different ways to specialize in combat. Some classes have their own Fighting Style feature and specific choice lists; this catalogue collects styles referenced by the Alternate Fighter and related character options. Check each style's prerequisites and the feature that grants it to see when you can choose it.

Some of the supplemental styles are uncommon. Learning one may require training from a dedicated master and DM approval.

entries.title: Character Options
entries.body:
# Building Your Character

Everything you need to create and customize a D&D 5e character.

**New to character building?** → **[[character-builder|Start with the step-by-step guide]]**

---

## The Five Building Blocks

### 1. Race

Your ancestry and heritage. Gives you special abilities and physical traits.

[[character-options/races|Browse Races →]]

**Examples:** Human, Elf, Dwarf, Halfling, Dragonborn, Tiefling

---

### 2. Class

Your role in the party. Defines your abilities and playstyle.

[[character-options/classes|Browse Classes →]]

**Examples:** [[character-options/classes/Artificer|Artificer]], [[character-options/classes/Fighter|Fighter]], [[character-options/classes/Wizard|Wizard]], [[character-options/classes/Cleric|Cleric]], [[character-options/classes/Rogue|Rogue]], [[character-options/classes/Barbarian|Barbarian]], [[character-options/classes/Warlock|Warlock]], [[character-options/classes/Sorcerer|Sorcerer]], [[character-options/classes/Paragon|Paragon]]

---

### 3. Subclass (Optional)

Specializes your class at a certain level (usually 3rd).

[[character-options/subclasses|Browse Subclasses →]]

**Examples:**

- [[character-options/classes/Fighter|Fighter]] → Champion
- [[character-options/classes/Wizard|Wizard]] → Evocation
- [[character-options/classes/Cleric|Cleric]] → Life
- [[character-options/classes/Warlock|Warlock]] → Fiend
- [[character-options/classes/Sorcerer|Sorcerer]] → Draconic
- [[character-options/classes/Artificer|Artificer]] → Battle Smith

---

### 4. Class-Specific Options (Optional)

Some classes have unique choice mechanics:

[[character-options/class-options|Browse Class Options →]]

**Examples:**

- **Warlock:** Eldritch Invocations (32 magical powers)
- **Sorcerer:** Metamagic (7 spell modifications)
- **Artificer:** Infuse Item (magical item crafting)

Fighting Styles are shared martial options available through features from multiple classes. [[character-options/fighting-styles/index|Browse the Fighting Styles catalogue]].

---

### 5. Feats & Background (Optional)

Special abilities and your character's story.

[[character-options/feats|Browse Feats →]] | [[character-options/backgrounds|Browse Backgrounds →]]

**Examples:** Grappler, Courageous, Acolyte, Martyr, Pilgrim

---

## All Character Options

| Option          | Purpose                   | Choose At                        |
| --------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Races           | Ancestry and heritage     | Character creation               |
| Classes         | Your main role            | Character creation               |
| Subclasses      | Role specialization       | 3rd level (usually)              |
| Backgrounds     | Your story                | Character creation               |
| Fighting Styles | Shared martial techniques | Class features and other options |
| Class Options   | Class-specific powers     | Varies by class                  |
| Feats           | Special abilities         | Levels 4, 8, 12, 16, 19          |
| Templates       | Special powers (optional) | Anytime (DM choice)              |

**Browse character options:** [[character-options/races|Races]], [[character-options/classes|Classes]], [[character-options/subclasses|Subclasses]], [[character-options/backgrounds|Backgrounds]], [[character-options/fighting-styles/index|Fighting Styles]], [[character-options/class-options|Class Options]], [[character-options/feats|Feats]], [[character-options/templates|Templates]]

![[character-options.base]]

---

## Class-Specific Choices

Some classes have unique mechanics for customization:

### Eldritch Invocations (Warlock)

32 magical powers you learn as your patron teaches you.

### Metamagic (Sorcerer)

7 ways to bend and modify your spells using Sorcery Points.

### Infuse Item (Artificer)

Craft magical items by imbuing objects with special properties.

---

## Spellcasters

If your class can cast spells, you need to know:

1. **Your class's spell list** — [[spells|Spells]] and each caster class page
2. **How to cast** — Casting time, components, concentration
3. **When to level up** — Get new spells at higher levels

**Full spell reference:** [[spells|Spells]]

---

## Starting at Level 1 vs Leveling Up

**At Level 1:**

- You have your race and class
- Most classes don't have a subclass yet (comes at level 3)
- Your DM might let you pick a feat

**As You Level Up:**

- Level 3: Pick your subclass (usually)
- Level 4+: Get ability score improvements or feats
- Level 5, 8, 11, etc.: Get more feats or ASIs (Ability Score Increases)
- Each level: Get class features and class-specific options
- Each class has unique level-ups (check your class page)

Ask your DM what level you're starting at.

---

## Quick Start

1. [[character-builder|Read the character building guide]]
2. Pick a [[character-options/races|race]]
3. Pick a [[character-options/classes|class]]
4. Decide on a [[character-options/subclasses|subclass]] (optional, comes at level 3)
5. Pick [[character-options/feats|feats]] (if your DM allows)

entries.title: Aengel
entries.summary: Medium celestial; speed 30 ft. and fly 30 ft.; +1 Strength,

frontmatter.title: Aengel
frontmatter.summary: Medium celestial; speed 30 ft. and fly 30 ft.; +1 Strength,

entries.body:
There are legends of angels falling from grace, thus losing their birth right and becoming something else. Such stories generally tell the tale of the most extreme of situations, but this is not always the case. Sometimes an angel starts to believe that the greater good can only be achieved outside the confines of heaven. Such angels don't fall but are removed from heaven's hierarchy. As a result, their granted powers gradually grow dim, and they become aengels.

> I had never seen such a variety of colors in one place. At least a dozen buckets were filled with hues of nature. He was dipping a massive brush in those buckets, dancing across a wide boulder, painting it with precise brushstrokes. My curiosity bested me and I approached him to ask what he was doing. He said that he was painting the enormous boulder as an expression of his feelings about being removed from heaven's hierarchy, so it could be seen from the heavens. I took him in and sheltered him from the evil that lurked outside the temple walls. Eventually, his curiosity about the world got the best of him, and he chose to leave this protection behind. I've missed him ever since. I sincerely hope that he can see the gray amid the black and white; that he can differentiate law and evil from all that lies in between.
>
> Saint Orea

## Looks of an Aengel

Aengels are genderless, their bodies may resemble a woman's, or a man's; both or neither. Their skin is perfectly smooth and varies in shade from dark green to dark orange. Their eyes have a slight glow, mostly white or light blue. They still carry the wings of an angel on their backs, but these wings are smaller than before.

## Life Without Blessings

It takes some time for most aengels to grow accustomed to a life without the blessings of deities and the protection of heaven. As aengels lose their clear perspective of the heavens, their memories of heaven start to fade. They lose their grip on magic, their excellent awareness, and their legendary capabilities. In fact, in the instant they leave heaven, they feel naked, disoriented, and lost before they start to adapt to their new life.

## Aengels in Society

Aengels seek perfection in everything, and are hence disappointed in the imperfect world that they are banished to. Because they are used to perfection, their criticisms of other creatures or their surroundings may sometimes be a bit harsh. As a result, they don't get along well with others, and are mostly forced to live a life of solitude.

## Aengel Names

Aengels almost always continue to use the names they had as angels. In some rare cases, they adopt new names, in accordance with their new earthly experiences.

**Original names:** Aoriel, Duvrael, Tivreel, Uminiel, Zeradel  
**New names:** Fartraveler, Justblade, Mindboggler, Skyseer, Swiftarrow

## Aengel Traits

Your angelic powers are dimmed and you are able to channel a small part of it, which offers a variety of abilities.

**Ability score increase:** Your Strength, Constitution, and Charisma scores each increase by 1.  
**Age:** Aengels are created as adults. You can't be aged by any means, and can't die of old age.  
**Alignment:** There are strict alignment restrictions for an aengel. They should always take actions that they believe to be in the interest of the greater good, paying no mind to rules and restrictions when necessary. In other words, they are either chaotic or neutral.

- **Evil.** When an aengel adopts the ways of evil, it becomes fallen and is no longer an aengel. When this happens in a game, the character either becomes a Fallen Angel, or becomes an NPC. The fate of the character is determined by the GM.
- **Lawful.** When an aengel starts to believe that the divine hierarchy works perfectly as they once did, and re-adopt the ways of the heavens, they can ascend back to heaven. When this happens in a game, the aengel becomes an angel once more, and the fate of the character is determined by the GM.

**Size:** Aengels stand between 6 and 7 feet tall and average about 220 pounds. Your size is Medium.  
**Speed:** Your base walking speed is 30 feet and you have a flying speed of 30 feet.  
**Languages:** You can speak, read, and write Common, Celestial, and one other language of your choice.

> [!info]- Aengelic Infusion
> When you hit with a spell or weapon attack, your attack deals an extra 1d4 radiant damage. This damage increases to 1d8 at 11th level and to 2d8 at 20th level.

> [!info]- Banished
> You are removed from heaven and now live in the material plane of existence.

> [!info]- Creature Type
> Your creature type is Celestial.

> [!info]- Darkvision
> You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

> [!info]- Dimmed Resistance
> When you fail a saving throw against a spell or another magical effect, you can choose to reroll the die. When you do so, you must take the second result. Once you use this feature, you must finish a long rest to use it again.

_From Corpus Angelus._

entries.title: Dragonborn
entries.summary: Medium size; speed 30 ft.; +2 STR, +1 CHA

frontmatter.title: Dragonborn
frontmatter.summary: Medium size; speed 30 ft.; +2 STR, +1 CHA

entries.body:
**Ability score increase:** +2 STR, +1 CHA  
**Age:** Young dragonborn grow quickly. They walk hours after hatching, attain the size and development of a 10-year-old human child by the age of 3, and reach adulthood by 15. They live to be around 80.  
**Alignment:** Dragonborn tend to extremes, making a conscious choice for one side or the other in the cosmic war between good and evil. Most dragonborn are good, but those who side with evil can be terrible villains.  
**Size:** Dragonborn are taller and heavier than humans, standing well over 6 feet tall and averaging almost 250 pounds. Your size is Medium.  
**Speed:** 30 feet  
**Languages:** You can speak, read, and write Common and Draconic. Draconic is thought to be one of the oldest languages and is often used in the study of magic. The language sounds harsh to most other creatures and includes numerous hard consonants and sibilants.

## Traits

> [!info]- Draconic Ancestry
> You have draconic ancestry. Choose one type of dragon from the Draconic Ancestry table. Your breath weapon and damage resistance are determined by the dragon type, as shown in the table.

> [!info]- Breath Weapon
> You can use your action to exhale destructive energy. Your draconic ancestry determines the size, shape, and damage type of the exhalation.
>
> When you use your breath weapon, each creature in the area of the exhalation must make a saving throw, the type of which is determined by your draconic ancestry. The DC for this saving throw equals 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus. A creature takes 2d6 damage on a failed save, and half as much damage on a successful one. The damage increases to 3d6 at 6th level, 4d6 at 11th level, and 5d6 at 16th level.
>
> After you use your breath weapon, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

> [!info]- Damage Resistance
> You have resistance to the damage type associated with your draconic ancestry.

entries.title: Dwarf
entries.summary: Medium size; speed 25 ft.; +2 CON

frontmatter.title: Dwarf
frontmatter.summary: Medium size; speed 25 ft.; +2 CON

entries.body:
**Ability score increase:** +2 CON  
**Age:** Dwarves mature at the same rate as humans, but they're considered young until they reach the age of 50. On average, they live about 350 years.  
**Alignment:** Most dwarves are lawful, believing firmly in the benefits of a well-ordered society. They tend toward good as well, with a strong sense of fair play and a belief that everyone deserves to share in the benefits of a just order.  
**Size:** Dwarves stand between 4 and 5 feet tall and average about 150 pounds. Your size is Medium.  
**Speed:** 25 feet  
**Languages:** You can speak, read, and write Common and Dwarvish. Dwarvish is full of hard consonants and guttural sounds, and those characteristics spill over into whatever other language a dwarf might speak.

## Traits

> [!info]- Darkvision
> You have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

> [!info]- Dwarven Resilience
> You have advantage on saving throws against poison, and you have resistance against poison damage.

> [!info]- Stonecunning
> Whenever you make an Intelligence (History) check related to the origin of stonework, you are considered proficient in the History skill and add double your proficiency bonus to the check, instead of your normal proficiency bonus.

> [!info]- Dwarven Combat Training
> You have proficiency with the battleaxe, handaxe, light hammer, and warhammer.

> [!info]- Tool Proficiency
> You gain proficiency with the artisan's tools of your choice: smith's tools, brewer's supplies, or mason's tools.

## Hill Dwarf

As a hill dwarf, you have keen senses, deep intuition, and remarkable resilience.

**Ability score increase:** +1 WIS

> [!info]- Dwarven Toughness
> Your hit point maximum increases by 1, and it increases by 1 every time you gain a level.

entries.title: Elf
entries.summary: Medium size; speed 30 ft.; +2 DEX

frontmatter.title: Elf
frontmatter.summary: Medium size; speed 30 ft.; +2 DEX

entries.body:
**Ability score increase:** +2 DEX  
**Age:** Although elves reach physical maturity at about the same age as humans, the elven understanding of adulthood goes beyond physical growth to encompass worldly experience. An elf typically claims adulthood and an adult name around the age of 100 and can live to be 750 years old.  
**Alignment:** Elves love freedom, variety, and self-expression, so they lean strongly toward the gentler aspects of chaos. They value and protect others' freedom as well as their own, and they are more often good than not.  
**Size:** Elves range from under 5 to over 6 feet tall and have slender builds. Your size is Medium.  
**Speed:** 30 feet  
**Languages:** You can speak, read, and write Common and Elvish. Elvish is fluid, with subtle intonations and intricate grammar. Elven literature is rich and varied, and their songs and poems are famous among other races. Many bards learn their language so they can add Elvish ballads to their repertoires.

## Traits

> [!info]- Darkvision
> You have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

> [!info]- Fey Ancestry
> You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic cannot put you to sleep.

> [!info]- Trance
> Elves do not need to sleep. Instead, they meditate deeply, remaining semiconscious, for 4 hours a day. (The Common word for such meditation is "trance.") While meditating, you can dream after a fashion; such dreams are actually mental exercises that have become reflexive through years of practice. After resting this way, you gain the same benefit that a human does from 8 hours of sleep.

> [!info]- Keen Senses
> You have proficiency in the Perception skill.

## High Elf

As a high elf, you have a keen mind and a mastery of at least the basics of magic. In many fantasy gaming worlds, there are two kinds of high elves. One type is haughty and reclusive, believing themselves to be superior to non-elves and even other elves. The other type is more common and more friendly, and often encountered among humans and other races.

**Ability score increase:** +1 INT

> [!info]- Elf Weapon Training
> You have proficiency with the longsword, shortsword, shortbow, and longbow.

> [!info]- High Elf Cantrip
> You know one cantrip of your choice form the wizard spell list. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for it.

> [!info]- Extra Language
> You can speak, read, and write one extra language of your choice.

entries.title: Gnome
entries.summary: Small size; speed 25 ft.; +2 INT

frontmatter.title: Gnome
frontmatter.summary: Small size; speed 25 ft.; +2 INT

entries.body:
**Ability score increase:** +2 INT  
**Age:** Gnomes mature at the same rate humans do, and most are expected to settle down into an adult life by around age 40. They can live 350 to almost 500 years.  
**Alignment:** Gnomes are most often good. Those who tend toward law are sages, engineers, researchers, scholars, investigators, or inventors. Those who tend toward chaos are minstrels, tricksters, wanderers, or fanciful jewelers. Gnomes are good-hearted, and even the tricksters among them are more playful than vicious.  
**Size:** Gnomes are between 3 and 4 feet tall and average about 40 pounds. Your size is Small.  
**Speed:** 25 feet  
**Languages:** You can speak, read, and write Common and Gnomish. The Gnomish language, which uses the Dwarvish script, is renowned for its technical treatises and its catalogs of knowledge about the natural world.

## Traits

> [!info]- Darkvision
> You have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

> [!info]- Gnome Cunning
> You have advantage on all Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws against magic.

## Rock Gnome

As a rock gnome, you have a natural inventiveness and hardiness beyond that of other gnomes.

**Ability score increase:** +1 CON

> [!info]- Artificer's Lore
> Whenever you make an Intelligence (History) check related to magic items, alchemical objects, or technological devices, you can add twice your proficiency bonus, instead of any proficiency bonus you normally apply.

> [!info]- Tinker
> You have proficiency with artisan's tools (tinker's tools). Using those tools, you can spend 1 hour and 10 gp worth of materials to construct a Tiny clockwork device (AC 5, 1 hp). The device ceases to function after 24 hours (unless you spend 1 hour repairing it to keep the device functioning), or when you use your action to dismantle it; at that time, you can reclaim the materials used to create it. You can have up to three such devices active at a time.
>
> When you create a device, choose one of the following options:
>
> Clockwork Toy: This toy is a clockwork animal, monster, or person, such as a frog, mouse, bird, dragon, or soldier. When placed on the ground, the toy moves 5 feet across the ground on each of your turns in a random direction. It makes noises as appropriate to the creature it represents.
>
> Fire Starter: The device produces a miniature flame, which you can use to light a candle, torch, or campfire. Using the device requires your action.
>
> Music Box: When opened, this music box plays a single song at a moderate volume. The box stops playing when it reaches the song's end or when it is closed.

**Age:** Half-elves mature at the same rate humans do and reach adulthood around the age of 20. They live much longer than humans, however, often exceeding 180 years.  
**Alignment:** Half-elves share the chaotic bent of their elven heritage. They value both personal freedom and creative expression, demonstrating neither love of leaders nor desire for followers. They chafe at rules, resent others' demands, and sometimes prove unreliable, or at least unpredictable.  
**Size:** Half-elves are about the same size as humans, ranging from 5 to 6 feet tall. Your size is Medium.  
**Speed:** 30 feet  
**Languages:** You can speak, read, and write Common, Elvish, and one extra language of your choice.

## Traits

> [!info]- Darkvision

entries.title: Half-Orc
entries.summary: Medium size; speed 30 ft.; +2 STR, +1 CON

frontmatter.title: Half-Orc
frontmatter.summary: Medium size; speed 30 ft.; +2 STR, +1 CON

entries.body:
**Ability score increase:** +2 STR, +1 CON  
**Age:** Half-orcs mature a little faster than humans, reaching adulthood around age 14. They age noticeably faster and rarely live longer than 75 years.  
**Alignment:** Half-orcs inherit a tendency toward chaos from their orc parents and are not strongly inclined toward good. Half-orcs raised among orcs and willing to live out their lives among them are usually evil.  
**Size:** Half-orcs are somewhat larger and bulkier than humans, and they range from 5 to well over 6 feet tall. Your size is Medium.  
**Speed:** 30 feet  
**Languages:** You can speak, read, and write Common and Orc. Orc is a harsh, grating language with hard consonants. It has no script of its own but is written in the Dwarvish script.

## Traits

> [!info]- Darkvision
> You have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

> [!info]- Savage Attacks
> When you score a critical hit with a melee weapon attack, you can roll one of the weapon's damage dice one additional time and add it to the extra damage of the critical hit.

> [!info]- Relentless Endurance
> When you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 hit point instead. you cannot use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

> [!info]- Menacing
> You gain proficiency in the Intimidation skill.

entries.title: Halfling
entries.summary: Small size; speed 25 ft.; +2 DEX

frontmatter.title: Halfling
frontmatter.summary: Small size; speed 25 ft.; +2 DEX

entries.body:
**Ability score increase:** +2 DEX  
**Age:** A halfling reaches adulthood at the age of 20 and generally lives into the middle of his or her second century.  
**Alignment:** Most halflings are lawful good. As a rule, they are good-hearted and kind, hate to see others in pain, and have no tolerance for oppression. They are also very orderly and traditional, leaning heavily on the support of their community and the comfort of their old ways.  
**Size:** Halflings average about 3 feet tall and weigh about 40 pounds. Your size is Small.  
**Speed:** 25 feet  
**Languages:** You can speak, read, and write Common and Halfling. The Halfling language isn't secret, but halflings are loath to share it with others. They write very little, so they don't have a rich body of literature. Their oral tradition, however, is very strong. Almost all halflings speak Common to converse with the people in whose lands they dwell or through which they are traveling.

## Traits

> [!info]- Brave
> You have advantage on saving throw against being frightened.

> [!info]- Halfling Nimbleness
> You can move through the space of any creature that is of a size larger than yours.

> [!info]- Lucky
> When you roll a 1 on the d20 for an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll.

## Lightfoot Halfling

As a lightfoot halfling, you can easily hide from notice, even using other people as cover. You're inclined to be affable and get along well with others. Lightfoots are more prone to wanderlust than other halflings, and often dwell alongside other races or take up a nomadic life.

**Ability score increase:** +1 CHA

> [!info]- Naturally Stealthy
> You can attempt to hide even when you are obscured only by a creature that is at least one size larger than you.

They are fond of sprinkling their speech with words borrowed from other tongues: Orc curses, Elvish musical expressions, Dwarvish military phrases, and so on.

# Character Races

Your **race** defines your ancestry, heritage, and heritage-based abilities.

Choose at character creation. This list is the races actually in the archive (SRD plus Corpus Angelus), not a full Player's Handbook catalog.

---

## What is a race?

Your race gives you:

- **Ability score bonuses** (boost to key attributes)
- **Special traits** (darkvision, flight, resistance, etc.)
- **Cultural background** (helps shape your character's story)
- **Speed and size** (affects combat and exploration)
- **Subraces** on some races (variants like High Elf vs Wood Elf)

---

Some races have **subraces** — cultural or magical variants listed on the race page.

**Examples:**
