entries.title: Keeper of Light
entries.summary: Ranger Conclave for the Ranger

frontmatter.title: Keeper of Light
frontmatter.summary: Ranger Conclave for the Ranger

entries.body:
Having a strong sense of enmity against darkness, some rangers choose to hunt evil creatures of the night. Be it celestial, a good spirit of nature, or another force, some form of magical light notices such a ranger and reaches out to them. The ranger and the light form a connection, and the light starts following the ranger like a companion, circling them in the shape of a shining ball.

## Features

> [!info]- The Shining Companion (level 3)
> At 3rd level, a ball of shining light attaches itself to you and you develop a bond with it. As a bonus action, you can call the light to appear right next to you, in your space.
>
> The ball of light is the same size as your head. It sheds bright light out to a range of 30 feet and dim light to an additional 30 feet.
>
> Once on each of your turns, when you hit a target with a weapon attack, the ball of light also hits the target with a ray of light, dealing 1d4 radiant damage. This damage increases to 1d8 at 11th level.
>
> The ball of light remains until you send it back as a bonus action or until you fall unconscious.

> [!info]- Keeper of Light Spells (level 3)
> Also starting at 3rd level, you learn an additional spell of 1st level or higher when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the following table. Each spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger spells you know.

## Keeper of Light spells

| Ranger level | Spells              |
| ------------ | ------------------- |
| 3rd          | [[Guiding Bolt]]    |
| 5th          | [[Continual Flame]] |
| 9th          | [[Daylight]]        |
| 13th         | [[Death Ward]]      |
| 17th         | [[Flame Strike]]    |

> [!info]- Lightplosion (level 7)
> Beginning at 7th level, you can cause the light you call to explode, requiring no action. Creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you that can see the explosion take 1d8 radiant damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or become blinded for 1 minute. A target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
>
> When you use this feature, the ball of light disappears and reappears right next to you, in your space after 1 minute.
>
> You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once), and you regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.

> [!info]- Protected by Light (level 11)
> At 11th level, the light that attached itself to you also provides you with protection. As a reaction, you can cause the light to cover your body. When you do so, you gain half cover until the start of your next turn.
>
> You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once), and you regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.

> [!info]- One with the Light (level 15)
> When you reach 15th level, you gain the ability to become one with the light you share a bond with, and travel together. If the light is next to you, you can use your bonus action to turn into light and travel to an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you.
>
> You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once) and regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.

_From Corpus Angelus._

entries.title: Chainbreaker
entries.summary: Roguish Archetype for the Rogue

frontmatter.title: Chainbreaker
frontmatter.summary: Roguish Archetype for the Rogue

entries.body:
Not all rogues are scoundrels, shady figures who lurk in back alleys, assassins, or wrong-doers... Some who understand the value of such things as honesty, innocence, and freedom choose a much more virtuous path; one that is far removed from that of their peers.

You understand the value of freedom and independence. You are a freedom fighter who defends the innocent and seeks to uphold justice. You stand against any and all in favor of slavery and stand in the way of all who disrespect the right of others to be free. You are, in every sense of the word, a chainbreaker.

## Features

> [!info]- For Freedom (level 3)
> When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, your swift fighting style keeps your enemies from slowing you down. You have advantage on ability checks or saving throws against being grappled, incapacitated, knocked prone, or restrained.
>
> Opportunity attacks against you are made with disadvantage.

> [!info]- Masters Shall Fall (level 3)
> Starting at 3rd level, you are fueled with a righteous fury against all creatures who own slaves. You have advantage on your attack rolls against slave masters. In addition, when you score a critical hit against them, you deal maximum damage.
>
> The GM determines whether a creature is a slave master or not. Creatures who charm or dominate others to make them act against their will, accept or support slavery, or act in any other wicked way to bolster slavery can be considered a slave master.

> [!info]- Freedom Fighter (level 9)
> At 9th level, your strikes against creatures that are grappling others get much better with practice. You have advantage on attack rolls against a creature that is grappling another one provided that you are neither the grappler nor the one being grappled. In addition, any hit you score against such a creature is a critical hit.

> [!info]- Voice of Freedom (level 13)
> At 13th level, your words of wisdom favoring freedom and cursing slavery start to influence people sincerely to adapt your values and fight for them. As an action, you speak your soulful words to grant your allies within 30 feet of you that can hear you the benefits of the freedom of movement spell. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest to use it again.

> [!info]- Savior (level 17)
> When you reach 17th level, you are held in high regard among the common folk, and are known by them as a savior and a well-known chainbreaker who fought injustice in society. You influence those around you. Any ally within 30 feet of you has advantage on their ability checks or saving throws against being grappled, incapacitated, knocked prone, or restrained.
>
> - You are immune to being grappled, knocked prone, and restrained.
>
> - Your speed increases by 10 feet.

_From Corpus Angelus._

entries.title: Divine Blade
entries.summary: Roguish Archetype for the Rogue

frontmatter.title: Divine Blade
frontmatter.summary: Roguish Archetype for the Rogue

entries.body:
Most assassins kill for the coin, and most thieves work to grow in fame and fortune. Divine Blades, on the other hand, have a divine calling. They seek and destroy their deities' enemies; the heretics and infidels. Temples may employ a divine blade following the same deity, or a divine blade can receive visions of the targets they must vanquish directly from their deity.

As a divine blade, you may be educated by a temple or another divine blade, or you can become aware of your abilities and your divine calling in another, perhaps mystical, way. Although most divine blades are followers of good deities, divine blades of evil forces are not unheard of.

## The Divine Quest

A divine blade is nothing without a divine quest. You can receive your quest from a temple, an emissary of your god, or a vision coming directly from your deity.

This quest can concern the elimination of a cult or a specific creature, the recovery of a precious relic from the hands of enemies, or something completely different, so long as all its details are approved by the GM.

## Features

> [!info]- The Avenger (level 3)
> When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you are known as "The Avenger". Most clergies know and share the identities of the avengers who serve the same deity as they do. While this allows you to receive help from your temple and the members of its clergy, the same reputation also causes you to have more enemies.

> [!info]- Bane of the Heretics (level 3)
> Starting at 3rd level, you can use your action to declare a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you a heretic. For 1 minute, your sneak attacks deal an extra 1d4 radiant damage to the heretic.
>
> Since such a declaration is a serious accusation, it must be made carefully. On a false declaration (if the creature is not an enemy of your deity or if your deity finds your declaration unjust), your attacks do not deal the extra damage because your deity does not grant you additional power. The GM determines whether or not your deity grants the power.
>
> When you reach certain levels in this class, the extra damage increases: At 9th level (1d6), at 13th level (1d8), and at 17th level (1d10).
>
> If the creature you declared a heretic is also a target given to you by your divine quest, the extra damage is doubled.
>
> If you make three wrong accusations in a week or try to abuse this power by making false accusations to learn others' intentions, your deity doubts your judgment and you cannot use this feature for the following week. The GM determines whether you abused this power or not.
>
> You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.

> [!info]- Seeker of the Heretics (level 9)
> At 9th level, you become an expert in snuffing out heretics. You can cast the [[Detect Evil and Good]], [[See Invisibility]], and [[Zone of Truth]] spells, requiring no material components. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells.
>
> Starting at 13th level, you can also cast the [[Locate Creature]] spell, requiring no material components.
>
> You can cast each spell once, and you regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.

> [!info]- No Sinner Runs Forever (level 13)
> Starting at 13th level, whenever you deal your Sneak Attack damage to a creature you accused of being a heretic with your Bane of the Heretics feature, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your Dexterity modifier + your proficiency bonus) or its speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn.

> [!info]- The High Avenger (level 17)
> When you reach 17th level, you earn the title: "The High Avenger". You become one of the most feared and most influential figures of your deity's clergy.
>
> Also starting at 17th level, you can use your action to channel divine energies to overwhelm a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you and that you declared a heretic within the last minute. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier) or be stunned for 1 minute. It can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a successful save.
>
> Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

_From Corpus Angelus._

entries.title: Thief
entries.summary: Roguish Archetype for the Rogue

frontmatter.title: Thief
frontmatter.summary: Roguish Archetype for the Rogue

entries.body:
_Roguish Archetype (Rogue subclass)_

You hone your skills in the larcenous arts. Burglars, bandits, cutpurses, and other criminals typically follow this archetype, but so do rogues who prefer to think of themselves as professional treasure seekers, explorers, delvers, and investigators. In addition to improving your agility and stealth, you learn skills useful for delving into ancient ruins, reading unfamiliar languages, and using magic items you normally couldn't employ.

## Features

> [!info]- Fast Hands (level 3)
> Starting at 3rd level, you can use the bonus action granted by your Cunning Action to make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, use your thieves' tools to disarm a trap or open a lock, or take the Use an Object action.

> [!info]- Second-Story Work (level 3)
> When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain the ability to climb faster than normal; climbing no longer costs you extra movement.
>
> In addition, when you make a running jump, the distance you cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Dexterity modifier.

> [!info]- Supreme Sneak (level 9)
> Starting at 9th level, you have advantage on a Dexterity (Stealth) check if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.

> [!info]- Use Magic Device (level 13)
> By 13th level, you have learned enough about the workings of magic that you can improvise the use of items even when they are not intended for you. You ignore all class, race, and level requirements on the use of magic items.

> [!info]- Thief's Reflexes (level 17)
> When you reach 17th level, you have become adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal initiative and your second turn at your initiative minus 10. You can't use this feature when you are surprised.

entries.title: Vigilante
entries.summary: Roguish Archetype for the Rogue

frontmatter.title: Vigilante
frontmatter.summary: Roguish Archetype for the Rogue

entries.body:
Most Vigilantes are investigators, bounty hunters, and local heroes. They work to punish crime and they value justice above practically anything else. Most vigilantes are villains and criminals in the eyes of those who prefer law over justice. It is common for a vigilante to work with people who share the same perspective about justice as they do, and it is also common for a vigilante to act as a judge, a jury, and an executioner all at once.

## Features

> [!info]- Vigilant (level 3)
> Starting at 3rd level, you are always aware of your surroundings. You gain a +5 bonus to your passive Perception and you gain proficiency in the Perception skill. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses this proficiency.

> [!info]- Criminal Investigator (level 3)
> When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Insight or Investigation skills if you are not already proficient. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of those proficiencies.

> [!info]- Vigilant Moves (level 3)
> Also, at 3rd level when you choose this archetype, you can make use of a variety of vigilant moves. You learn two moves at this level. You learn one additional move of your choice when you reach 10th, 14th, and 18th level. You can choose from the styles below:
>
> **Adrenaline Rush.** You enter a state of exhilaration. For 1 minute, your carrying capacity is doubled and having 0 hit points doesn't knock you unconscious. You must still make death saving throws, and you suffer the normal effects of taking damage while at 0 hit points.
>
> Once you use this feature, you must finish a long rest to use it again.
>
> **Bleeding Cut.** After making a successful Sneak Attack against a creature, you can choose to leave the weapon that you used to attack inside the creature. The creature has -1d4 penalty on its next Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution saving throw (the first one it makes). When it makes the saving throw, the weapon falls to ground out of the creature, ending the effect. The creature can also take the weapon out of its wound as an action, ending the effect by doing so.
>
> **Crisis Negotiation.** You can rescue a grappled creature by striking the grappler. If you successfully hit a grappler with a Sneak Attack, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC is equal to 8 + your Dexterity modifier + your proficiency bonus), or be forced to release its hold and thus the grapple ends.
>
> **Innocuous Strike.** When you make a successful Sneak Attack against a creature, you can choose to deal no damage to the creature and to reduce its speed by 10 feet for 1 minute instead. Consecutive uses of this effect do not stack.
>
> **Pinning Strike.** During an encounter, when you make your first Sneak Attack against a creature, the creature's speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn.
>
> **Symbol of Fear.** As an action, you make a ranged weapon attack that requires no roll to an unoccupied space right next to a creature. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC is equal to 8 + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus), or be frightened for 1 minute. While frightened by this feature, the source of the creature's fear is you, or the thrown weapon or ammunition if the creature can't see you.
>
> **Taking Initiative.** As an action, you can change a willing ally's initiative and make it equal to one less than your own.

> [!info]- Denying the Unjust (level 9)
> At 9th level, you learn how to deny the unrighteous advantage. If a creature that you are aware of is making an attack with advantage, you can make one weapon attack against that creature as a reaction before it attacks. If your attack hits, the target makes its attack without advantage.

> [!info]- Cautious Steps (level 13)
> Starting at 13th level, you can adjust your movement considering the actions of others. When a creature within 60 feet of you that you are aware of takes an action, you can immediately move up to 10 feet using your speed without using your reaction before the creature's action ends. This extra movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. You can use this feature once per turn.

> [!info]- Verdict (level 17)
> At 17th level, you can study a creature as a bonus action. When you do so, the Sneak Attack damage you deal to that creature increases by 2d6 for 1 minute.
>
> Also, you gain the ability to enforce your judgment over the guilty. As an action, you speak of the crimes of a creature within 30 feet of you, also stating its punishment. As a vigilante, you are responsible for giving a just punishment and can discuss what that entails with the GM. Even if the creature can't understand or hear you, it knows that it is being accused if it is aware of you in any way. If the creature isn't aware of you or didn't commit any crimes that you know of, this ability has no effect. Otherwise, the creature has two options:
>
> **Plead Guilty.** The creature surrenders and chooses not to take any hostile actions against you and your allies. It accepts the punishment of the vigilante.
>
> **Refusing the Verdict.** The creature refuses to comply. It must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC is equal to 8 + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus) or is overwhelmed with the need to clear its name. The creature can't retreat from a fight with you until you retreat or fall unconscious. The creature can repeat its saving throw once it drops below 50 hit points and repeat it again with advantage once it drops below 25 hit points. This effect ends if the creature ends its turn 300 feet away from you.
>
> All creatures that are aware of your verdict have advantage on attack rolls against the accused creature.

_From Corpus Angelus._

_Sorcerous Origin (Sorcerer subclass)_

Your innate magic comes from draconic magic that was mingled with your blood or that of your ancestors. Most often, sorcerers with this origin trace their descent back to a mighty sorcerer of ancient times who made a bargain with a dragon or who might even have claimed a dragon parent. Some of these bloodlines are well established in the world, but most are obscure. Any given sorcerer could be the first of a new bloodline, as a result of a pact or some other exceptional circumstance.

> [!info]- Draconic Resilience (level 1)

>

> Starting at 6th level, when you cast a spell that deals damage of the type associated with your draconic ancestry, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell. At the same time, you can spend 1 sorcery point to gain resistance to that damage type for 1 hour.

> [!info]- Dragon Wings (level 14)
> At 14th level, you gain the ability to sprout a pair of dragon wings from your back, gaining a flying speed equal to your current speed. You can create these wings as a bonus action on your turn. They last until you dismiss them as a bonus action on your turn.
>
> You can't manifest your wings while wearing armor unless the armor is made to accommodate them, and clothing not made to accommodate your wings might be destroyed when you manifest them.

> [!info]- Draconic Presence (level 18)
> Beginning at 18th level, you can channel the dread presence of your dragon ancestor, causing those around you to become awestruck or frightened. As an action, you can spend 5 sorcery points to draw on this power and exude an aura of awe or fear (your choice) to a distance of 60 feet. For 1 minute or until you lose your concentration (as if you were casting a concentration spell), each hostile creature that starts its turn in this aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed (if you chose awe) or frightened (if you chose fear) until the aura ends. A creature that succeeds on this saving throw is immune to your aura for 24 hours.

entries.title: Prismatic Sorcerer
entries.summary: Sorcerous Origin for the Sorcerer

frontmatter.title: Prismatic Sorcerer
frontmatter.summary: Sorcerous Origin for the Sorcerer

entries.body:
You are of an arcane bloodline, blessed by a good celestial, native to a plane of light. You have the power of light coursing through your veins as a result. When you want, you can shine bright with the purest light of varying colors.

Each color has a different meaning and offers a different blessing; all aimed at turning you into a potent agent of good to be feared and respected.

## Features

> [!info]- Prismagic (level 1)
> Starting at 1st level, as you gain the ability to cast spells, you realize that each color of the prism represents a different school of magic. You can choose to alter the color of your spells as you wish. For example, you can cast violet fire bolts.
>
> In addition, you choose a color (and a spell school) at the end of each long rest, the DC for the spells of which increases by 1 until you finish a long rest.

### Prismatic spectrum

| Color  | Spell school  |
| ------ | ------------- |
| Red    | Evocation     |
| Orange | Enchantment   |
| Yellow | Illusion      |
| Green  | Necromancy    |
| Blue   | Conjuration   |
| Indigo | Abjuration    |
| Violet | Transmutation |
| White  | Divination    |

> [!info]- Color Focus (level 1)
> Starting at 1st level, when you choose the same color as the one you chose on the previous day using the Prismagic feature, you gain additional sorcery points equal to your proficiency bonus until you finish a long rest.

> [!info]- Color Expert (level 6)
> Starting at 6th level, when you cast a spell that deals damage, you can change its damage type as you wish. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. You can gain an extra use of this feature by expending 3 sorcery points.
>
> You regain any expended uses after you finish a long rest.

> [!info]- Advanced Prismagic (level 14)
> At 14th level, your Prismagic feature grows stronger. You gain the following benefits while you are under the influence of different colors.
>
> **Red.** Your evocation spells deal 1d6 bonus damage.
>
> **Orange.** Your spell save DC for enchantment spells increases by 2 instead of 1.
>
> **Yellow.** The duration of your illusion spells is doubled.
>
> **Green.** When you raise or create a creature, as in the raise dead spell, you can raise or create one additional creature.
>
> **Blue.** The duration of your conjuration spells is doubled.
>
> **Indigo.** You can cast abjuration spells whose casting time is 1 action as a bonus action instead.
>
> **Violet.** Your spell save DC for transmutation spells increases by 2, instead of 1.
>
> **White.** Creatures have disadvantage on saving throws against your divination spells.

> [!info]- Prismatic Radiance (level 18)
> Starting at 18th level, you can use your action to spend 9 sorcery points and radiate a bright light in a 60-foot-radius sphere centered on you, consisting of each color of your prismatic spectrum. Creatures caught in the light must succeed on a Constitution saving throw with disadvantage or be affected by the prismatic spray spell.

_From Corpus Angelus._

entries.title: Starborn
entries.summary: Sorcerous Origin for the Sorcerer

frontmatter.title: Starborn
frontmatter.summary: Sorcerous Origin for the Sorcerer

entries.body:
You carry the heavenly energy of stars in your veins and your innate magic comes from the arcane forces woven around the stars. Whether you are somehow related to a star incarnate, were blessed by a divine being native to the stars, or found this gift through your own endeavors in the field of star magic; you are now of the stars. You shine bright with the gift bestowed upon you and illuminate the darkness.

## Features

> [!info]- Child of the Stars (level 1)
> Starting when you choose this sorcerous origin at 1st level, you can always find your way by looking at the night sky. You always know which way is north, provided that you can see the stars. In addition, when you finish a long rest under a starry night sky, you have advantage on your first attack roll, ability check, or saving throw (whichever happens first) until you finish another long rest.

> [!info]- Starstrike (level 1)
> Starting at 1st level, stars watch over you and help you in combat. Once per turn, when you hit a target with a spell attack, a shiny ray of radiant star energy shoots out from your fingertips and hits your target, dealing an extra 1d4 radiant damage. If the spell attack has more than one target, you choose which target takes the additional damage.
>
> This additional damage increases to 2d4 at 5th level, 3d4 at 10th level, 4d4 at 15th level and 5d4 at 20th level.

> [!info]- Starrain (level 6)
> Starting at 6th level, you can charm others with your innate starlight. As an action, you can choose a point within 120 feet of you to fill a 30-foot radius centered on that point with stardust, which falls like rain for the duration. When a creature enters the area for the first time or ends its turn there, it must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be charmed by you until they leave the affected area. The rain of stardust lasts for 1 minute or until you fall unconscious. In addition, creatures who failed the Charisma saving throw can't benefit from being invisible.
>
> Creatures in the area have disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
>
> Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest to use it again.

> [!info]- Magic of Starlight (level 6)
> Beginning at 6th level, you are blessed with the magic of starlight. When you cast a damage-dealing spell, you can choose to deal radiant damage instead of the spell's normal damage type. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.

> [!info]- Starshine (level 14)
> Starting at 14th level, you are able to channel your innate starlight to emanate radiant energy. As an action, you transform into a silhouette of bright light for 1 minute. You illuminate your surroundings; shedding bright light in a 50-foot radius and dim light for an additional 50 feet. You also gain immunity to radiant damage for the duration. Also, when a creature enters a space within 5 feet of you for the first time or ends its turn there, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be blinded for 1 minute or until they are 30 feet away from you. Additionally, your spell attacks deal an extra 2d6 radiant damage for the duration.
>
> Once you use this feature, you must finish a long rest to use it again.

> [!info]- Starfall (level 18)
> Beginning at 18th level, stars fall to come to your aid. When you take damage from a creature within 60 feet of you while your current hit points are below half of your hit point maximum, a star falls and hits the creature. The creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or take 1d8 radiant damage plus 1d8 bludgeoning damage.
>
> In addition, once per week, when you drop to 0 hit points, stars fall to avenge you. When this happens, each enemy within 120 feet of you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or take 6d8 radiant damage plus 6d8 bludgeoning damage.

_From Corpus Angelus._

entries.title: The Knight Dragon Bloodline
entries.summary: Sorcerous Origin for the Sorcerer

frontmatter.title: The Knight Dragon Bloodline
frontmatter.summary: Sorcerous Origin for the Sorcerer

entries.body:
Your innate magic comes from the heavenly might of Knight Dragons. These knights are brave dragons who reside in heaven and embody ideas of chivalry.

There are many ways one becomes a sorcerer of this bloodline; for instance, a knight dragon can gift the bloodline to those they deem worthy, or one can be a descendant of a dragon. Like the dragons they represent, most sorcerers of this bloodline have a knack for martial arts, enjoy battle, and live in pursuit of the greater good.

## Features

> [!info]- Heavenly Warrior Ancestor (level 1)
> You can speak, read, and write Celestial and Draconic. Also, you are proficient with one martial weapon and one armor of your choice.

> [!info]- Sword of the Knight Dragon (level 1)
> At 1st level, you feel you're under the watchful eye of your ancestors. Once per turn, when you hit a target with a weapon attack, a golden sword appears in the air and revolves around you. Creatures within 5 feet of you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take slashing damage equal to half your sorcerer level (minimum of one damage).

> [!info]- Armory of the Knight Dragon (level 6)
> At 6th level, you can use your action to conjure up to three weapons and armor from the armory of your knight dragon ancestor (for example a longsword, a shield, and a breastplate; or a halberd, a battleaxe, and a plate), which immediately appear in your hand or on your body. You must be proficient with the armor and the weapon to conjure it. Weapons and armor made up of more than one piece (e.g. gauntlets) cannot be conjured using this feature.
>
> The weapons and armor conjured in this way are magic weapons, and they are in gold instead of their regular color. When you attack with a conjured weapon, you can use Charisma instead of Strength or Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls you make. The conjured weapons are also larger than usual, which increases their weapon damage by 1d6.
>
> A conjured weapon deals an extra 1d6 radiant damage on a hit when you reach 14th level, and becomes a +2 weapon when you reach 18th level in this class.
>
> A conjured armor and shield also becomes +1 when you reach 10th level, and +2 when you reach 14th level, and +3 when you reach 18th level in this class.
>
> The conjured weapon and armor remain until you dismiss them as a bonus action, or until you fall unconscious.

> [!info]- Knightly Metamagic (level 6)
> Starting at 6th level, when you take the Attack action to make weapon attacks, you can spend 2 sorcery points to make another weapon attack once per turn.

> [!info]- Extra Attack (level 14)
> Beginning at 14th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

> [!info]- The Dragon Within (level 14)
> At 14th level, you sprout draconic wings and gain a flying speed of 30 feet.

> [!info]- Will of the Knight Dragon (level 18)
> Starting at 18th level, you refuse to fall before your enemies do. When you drop to 0 hit points, you start to regain a number of hit points equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one hit point) at the start of each of your turns for 1 minute.
>
> Once this effect takes place, you must finish a short or long rest for it to do so again.

_From Corpus Angelus._

entries.title: Tamer Training Paradigms
entries.body:
# Tamer Training Paradigms

At 3rd level, a Tamer chooses a Training Paradigm. Each paradigm grants features at 3rd, 7th, 10th, and 14th level, with its 7th-level feature improving at 18th level.

- [[character-options/subclasses/Tamer/Leader|Leader]] — Coordinate companions through encouragement and tactical direction.
- [[character-options/subclasses/Tamer/Infuser|Infuser]] — Empower companions with primordial elements.
- [[character-options/subclasses/Tamer/Necromancer|Necromancer]] — Bind and empower undead companions.
- [[character-options/subclasses/Tamer/Splicer|Splicer]] — Modify companions through biomancy.

entries.body:
# Infuser

Infusers meld primordial elemental power with their companions.

## Infuse

_3rd-level Infuser feature_

After a long rest, infuse each companion with acid, cold, fire, or lightning. The first time it hits a target on its turn, it deals 1d4 additional damage of that type.

The damage becomes 1d6 at 6th level, 1d8 at 10th level, and 1d10 at 14th level.

## Infuser Spells

These spells count as Tamer spells and do not count against spells known. Appendix B spells remain unimported.

| Tamer Level | Spells                                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| 3rd         | _hellish rebuke_, _peppermint plate_ (Appendix B) |
| 5th         | _eelskin_ (Appendix B), _riptide_ (Appendix B)    |
| 9th         | _protection from energy_, _wind wall_             |
| 13th        | _control water_, _fire shield_                    |
| 17th        | _feverskin_ (Appendix B), _wall of stone_         |

## Elemental Discharge

_7th-level Infuser feature_

When infusing a companion, it gains an action corresponding to its element. The save DC equals your Tamer spell save DC.

- **Acid: Caustic Mist.** A 20-foot cube around the companion lasts for one minute. Creatures entering or starting there make Constitution saves or take 4d4 acid damage, half on success.
- **Cold: Snap Freeze.** Creatures in a 10-foot-radius sphere make Constitution saves, taking 4d8 cold damage and suffering halved speed for one round on failure.
- **Fire: Flametongue.** Creatures in a 25-foot cone make Dexterity saves, taking 6d6 fire damage on failure, half on success.
- **Lightning: Sparkstep.** Creatures in a 10-foot-radius sphere make Dexterity saves, taking 4d6 lightning damage on failure, half on success. The companion can then fly 30 feet.

Once used, the companion cannot use its elemental action again until you finish a short or long rest. At 18th level, it can use the action twice before a rest.

## Primordial Shield

_10th-level Infuser feature_

A companion gains resistance to its infused element. When it takes damage of that type, use your reaction to grant immunity to that damage until the start of your next turn. Once used, regain after a short or long rest.

## Unstable Fusion

_14th-level Infuser feature_

As an action, infuse a companion with a second element for one minute. It gains both infusions, discharges, and shields. Once used, regain after a long rest.

entries.body:
# Leader

Leaders use encouragement, gestures, game plans, or telepathic reinforcement to push companions beyond their normal limits.

## Inspire

_3rd-level Leader feature_

As an action, inspire your companion. Until the beginning of your next turn, whenever it makes a saving throw or attack roll, it can add a die to the result.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Tamer spellcasting ability modifier, minimum once. Regain all uses after a short or long rest.

The die is a d6, becoming a d8 at 6th level, d10 at 10th level, and d12 at 14th level.

## Leader Spells

These spells count as Tamer spells and do not count against spells known. Appendix B spells remain unimported.

| Tamer Level | Spells                                          |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| 3rd         | _divine favor_, _protection from evil and good_ |
| 5th         | _inequality_ (Appendix B), _warding bond_       |
| 9th         | _beacon of hope_, _haste_                       |
| 13th        | _death ward_, _freedom of movement_             |
| 17th        | _dispel evil and good_, _endure_ (Appendix B)   |

## Action Burst

_7th-level Leader feature_

When you command your companion, it can take one additional action on its turn. Once a companion benefits from this feature, it must finish a short or long rest before benefiting again.

At 18th level, companions can benefit twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.

## Leader's Fortitude

_10th-level Leader feature_

When an attacker you can see hits your companion, use both your reaction and your companion's reaction to halve the attack's damage.

## Combo

_14th-level Leader feature_

As an action, summon a second companion. When you command your companions, give each a different command. They act in an order of your choice after your turn.

Once used, this feature returns after a long rest.

entries.body:
# Necromancer

Necromancers manipulate life force and create undead companions through taming magic.

## Life Hack

_3rd-level Necromancer feature_

Once per turn when a companion hits a creature, you can command it to shed life force. It takes 1d4 necrotic damage, gains that many temporary hit points, and deals that much additional necrotic damage to its target.

The damage becomes 1d6 at 6th level, 1d8 at 10th level, and 1d10 at 14th level.

## Post-Mortem

_3rd-level Necromancer feature_

Within one minute of a creature dying, you can attempt to tame it. Its soul makes a Charisma saving throw against your Tamer spell save DC. Humanoids and giants do not automatically succeed. On a failure, its soul binds to its body, its type becomes undead, and it becomes your companion.

## Necromancer Spells

These spells count as Tamer spells and do not count against spells known. Appendix B spells remain unimported.

| Tamer Level | Spells                                          |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| 3rd         | _false life_, _inflict wounds_                  |
| 5th         | _blindness/deafness_, _ray of enfeeblement_     |
| 9th         | _influenza_ (Appendix B), _vampiric touch_      |
| 13th        | _confusion_, _death ward_                       |
| 17th        | _bone cage_ (Appendix B), _endure_ (Appendix B) |

## Animate Dead

_7th-level Necromancer feature_

You learn _animate dead_, always have it prepared, and can cast it once without a spell slot. Regain this use after a long rest.

At 18th level, creatures animated through this feature can use ghast statistics for Medium or smaller corpses or minotaur skeleton statistics for larger corpses. You can maintain control of one such creature per casting.

## Enervate

_10th-level Necromancer feature_

As an action while a summoned companion is within 100 feet, deal necrotic damage to it up to twice your Tamer level and regain that many hit points. Alternatively, take the damage yourself and restore that many hit points to the companion.

## Aura of Undeath

_14th-level Necromancer feature_

As an action, give a companion a 15-foot aura for one minute. Creatures in the aura make Constitution saves or take 4d8 necrotic damage, while the companion gains temporary hit points equal to half the damage dealt.

The companion also remains at 1 hit point instead of falling unconscious when reduced to 0 hit points, gaining failed death saves. It dies if it reaches the specified failed-save limit. After one use, regain after a long rest.

entries.body:
# Splicer

Splicers alter companion physiology through biomancy and surgical augmentation.

## Augment

_3rd-level Splicer feature_

You gain 3 splicer points and gain 1 additional point each time you gain a Tamer level. Spend points to modify companions. Augments take effect after the next long rest.

If a companion is released, it loses its augments and the points are refunded. You also gain proficiency with surgeon's tools and can remove all augments from a companion during one hour of work.

## Splicer Augments

| Cost | Augments                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---: | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
|    0 | Water Breathing                                                                                                                                                                      |
|    1 | Amphibious, Darkvision, Extra Limb, Fins & Webbing, Illumination, Keen Hearing, Keen Sight, Keen Smell, Powerful Build, Prehensile Tail, Slippery, Sure-Footed, Web Sense + Web Walk |
|    2 | Burrowing Claws, Long Limbed, Mimicry, Natural Armour, Poisonous Touch, Spider Climb                                                                                                 |
|    3 | Camouflage, Corrosive Touch, Tremorsense, Wings                                                                                                                                      |
|    4 | Blindsight + Echolocation, Decaying Touch, Flyby, Growth Hormone                                                                                                                     |

Each augment's limitations and repeated-use rules follow the supplied Tamer source.

## Splicer Spells

These spells count as Tamer spells and do not count against spells known. Appendix B spells remain unimported.

| Tamer Level | Spells                                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| 3rd         | _chameleon skin_ (Appendix B), _disguise self_    |
| 5th         | _barkskin_, _eelskin_ (Appendix B)                |
| 9th         | _mass leech_ (Appendix B), _zippit!_ (Appendix B) |
| 13th        | _frogskin_ (Appendix B), _stoneskin_              |
| 17th        | _contagion_, _feverskin_ (Appendix B)             |

## Modular Upgrades

_7th-level Splicer feature_

At the start of a long rest, choose one upgrade for each companion. It completes at the end of the rest. The save DC equals your Tamer spell save DC.

- **Compelling Plumage:** Creatures in a 25-foot cone can be charmed and incapacitated until the effect ends.
- **Phosphoburst:** Creatures in a 10-foot sphere make Constitution saves or take 2d10 radiant damage and become blinded.
- **Poison Web:** A 20-foot cube becomes webbed; creatures can become restrained and take poison damage.
- **Sirenshriek:** Creatures in a 15-foot sphere make Intelligence saves or take 3d8 psychic damage and lose concentration.

A companion can use an upgrade once before a short or long rest. At 18th level, it can use the action twice before a rest.

## Battlefield Harvester

_10th-level Splicer feature_

As an action, command a companion to consume the corpse of a non-swarm creature dead less than one minute. Choose a resistance, immunity, or condition immunity from the corpse. All companions gain the corresponding resistance or condition immunity until this feature is used again.

## Adrenal Overload

_14th-level Splicer feature_

As an action, a companion grows to Huge size, gains temporary hit points equal to ten times your Tamer level, has Strength 22 if not higher, gains Athletics proficiency, and gains a three-attack appendage Multiattack. The effect lasts one minute; afterward the companion falls unconscious for 1d4 hours and gains two exhaustion levels. Regain after a long rest.

frontmatter.title: Path of the Fleshweaver
frontmatter.summary: Crafts, grafts, and augments stitchwork undead minions

entries.body:
# Path of the Fleshweaver

Fleshweavers harvest the remains of fallen creatures to build and refine specialized undead servants. Their stitchwork minions are adaptable creations, enhanced with grafts and necrotic energy.

## Tool Proficiency

_3rd-level Path of the Fleshweaver feature_

You gain proficiency with leatherworker's tools. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of artisan's tools of your choice.

## Stitchwork Minion

_3rd-level Path of the Fleshweaver feature_

You can craft specialized Undead servants called stitchwork minions from corpses. These minions are friendly to you and your companions. Their statistics appear below; they use your proficiency bonus (PB) in several places.

You can control a number of stitchwork minions equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down). If you create another minion over your maximum, one minion of your choice is destroyed. You share a telepathic link with your minions while they remain within 120 feet of you. Through this link, you can issue commands to any number of your minions as a bonus action, giving individual commands or one command to all of them.

In combat, your stitchwork minions share your initiative count, and each takes its turn after yours. A minion follows your most recent command until it completes the task, receives a new command, or can no longer fulfill the order. If it has no command it can meaningfully act on, it takes the Dodge action.

If a minion dies, it crumbles to dust after 1 hour and is destroyed. Until it is destroyed, you can reanimate it using your leatherworker's tools. Spend 1 minute within 5 feet of the minion and expend a 1st-level or higher spell slot; it is reanimated, regains all its hit points, and returns under your control.

## Fleshweaving

_3rd-level Path of the Fleshweaver feature_

You can harvest body parts from corpses and graft them onto your stitchwork minions. Each minion can bear one graft at 3rd level, two grafts at 6th level, and three grafts at 10th level. See [[#Stitchwork Minion Crafting]] below.

### Corpse Satchel

As part of your fleshweaving rituals, you can craft a special extradimensional container called a corpse satchel. It opens a subdimensional fold within the Mortis Veil, accessible only to you, and stores remains for future minion creation or grafting.

You must spend 1 hour crafting the satchel with leatherworker's tools; you can do so during a short or long rest. It takes the form of a leather bag, satchel, pack, or other container of your choice. At the GM's discretion, only corpses and harvested body parts can be stored inside. It can hold up to 500 pounds of these materials, suspended in time and insulated from decay. At 13th level, you can craft a satchel that holds up to 1,000 pounds.

You can retrieve or store one corpse or part as an action. If the satchel is destroyed or lost, its contents are shunted into the Void and lost forever. You can have only one functioning corpse satchel at a time. If it is destroyed or replaced, all contents are instantly lost and unusable.

## Mortis Enhancement

_6th-level Path of the Fleshweaver feature_

You can channel necrotic energy into your creations to make them specialized battlefield threats.

### Augmentation

As a bonus action, expend 2 mortis points to empower a stitchwork minion for 1 minute with one of the following augmentations:

- **Artillerist.** Arcane energy builds behind the minion's gaze. It gains the following action:
  - **Arcane Bolt.** _Ranged Spell Attack:_ your spell attack modifier to hit, range 60 feet, one target. _Hit:_ 2 × PB force damage.
- **Brute.** The minion grows bristling armor of spikes and bone, gaining a +2 bonus to AC.
- **Soldier.** When the minion takes the Attack action, it can make an additional attack as a bonus action.
- **Stalker.** The minion's walking speed increases by 10 feet, and it can take the Dash or Disengage action as a bonus action on each of its turns.

A minion can benefit from only one augmentation at a time; applying a new one ends the previous effect.

### Healing

When you cast a spell that deals necrotic damage, you can choose to target your stitchwork minions or affect minions within the spell's area of effect. Instead of taking damage, each affected minion regains hit points equal to half the necrotic damage the spell would have dealt, ignoring resistances and immunities.

Starting at 13th level, when you use this feature, you can expend 2 mortis points per affected minion to restore hit points equal to the full amount of necrotic damage the spell would have dealt to it, instead of half.

## Master Fleshweaving

_10th-level Path of the Fleshweaver feature_

### Mortis Bond

Your newly crafted minions gain the following benefits:

- They add your proficiency bonus to any ability check or saving throw they make.
- When they deal necrotic damage, they ignore resistance to necrotic damage and treat immunity as resistance.

Additionally, when a minion hits with or is hit by an attack, it can use its reaction to enable you to use a Veil Technique that requires a reaction, using the minion as the source of the technique, even if you have used a Veil Technique this turn. You must expend 2 mortis points in addition to the technique's normal cost. After using a technique through a minion this way, you can't do so again until the start of your next turn.

### Enhanced Augmentation

When you use Augmentation, you can expend 3 additional mortis points (5 total) to extend its duration to 1 hour. You can extend a duration this way a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum once), regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Additionally, when you craft a stitchwork minion or over the course of a long rest, you can use one of its available graft slots to permanently enhance it with one augmentation from Augmentation. This effect is always active until the minion is destroyed. While permanently augmented, the minion can't benefit from that same augmentation again, and one of its available graft slots is permanently used. A minion can have only one permanent augmentation in this way.

## Wraithbound Army

_18th-level Path of the Fleshweaver feature_

As an action, expend mortis points to transform up to three of your stitchwork minions into wraithbound minions for 1 minute, turning their flesh into spectral essence. The cost is 2 mortis points per minion. Each transformed minion gains the following benefits:

- **Death Wail.** When the minion hits a creature with a melee weapon attack, it can use a bonus action to force that creature to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature is frightened until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, or after the duration ends for it, the creature is immune to Death Wail for 24 hours.
- **Feed on Fear.** The minion has advantage on attacks against frightened creatures, and its attacks deal an extra PB psychic damage on a hit against them.
- **Phantom Limbs.** The minion can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. If it ends its turn inside a creature or object, it takes 1d10 force damage and is shunted to the last unoccupied space it left. It ignores nonmagical difficult terrain, and opportunity attacks against it have disadvantage.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 6 mortis points to use it again.

## Stitchwork Minion Crafting

To create a stitchwork minion, perform a necromantic ritual on the corpse of a creature that died within the last 24 hours. The ritual takes 1 hour and can be performed during a short or long rest.

### Minion traits

When crafting a minion, it gains a trait based on the creature type of the corpse used:

| Creature Type | Trait                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Aberration    | **Alien Anatomy.** The minion has advantage on saving throws against being grappled, restrained, or paralyzed. It can move through spaces as narrow as 1 foot wide without squeezing, and opportunity attacks against it have disadvantage.                                                    |
| Beast         | **Pack Tactics.** The minion has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of its allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.                                                                                                               |
| Celestial     | **Sanctified Form.** The minion has advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened. Undead and Fiends of its choice within 5 feet have disadvantage on attack rolls against it if they can see it.                                                                             |
| Dragon        | **Draconic Scales.** The minion's AC increases by 1. **Wings.** The minion has a flying speed equal to its walking speed.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Elemental     | **Elemental Strike.** The minion's melee weapon attacks deal an extra PB acid, cold, fire, or lightning damage (choose a type appropriate to the original Elemental).                                                                                                                          |
| Fey           | **Trickster's Presence.** Hostile creatures within 5 feet of the minion have disadvantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.                                                                                                                                                |
| Fiend         | **Hellbrand Tormentor.** The first time the minion hits a creature with a melee attack, that creature has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes before the end of its next turn. Once the effect ends for a creature, it is immune to this minion's Hellbrand Tormentor for 24 hours. |
| Giant         | **Giant's Might.** The minion has advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. The first time it hits with a melee weapon attack on its turn, it deals an extra PB bludgeoning damage.                                                                                             |
| Humanoid      | **Martial Prowess.** The minion is proficient with simple and martial weapons and gains a +1 bonus to weapon attack and damage rolls. Weapon attacks use your spell attack modifier to hit.                                                                                                    |
| Monstrosity   | **Unnatural Bulk.** The minion counts as one size larger when determining its carrying capacity and the size of creatures it can grapple. It has advantage on saving throws to resist being knocked prone or moved.                                                                            |
| Undead        | **Rotting Grasp (1/Day).** As a bonus action when the minion hits a creature with a melee weapon attack, it can force the target to make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, the creature can't regain hit points until the start of your next turn.         |

The minion's size is equal to the size of the corpse used in the ritual and determines its Hit Die: Small uses d6s, Medium uses d8s, and Large uses d10s. You can use corpses of the following types and sizes based on your thanatomancer level:

| Thanatomancer Level | Sizes           | Creature Types                          |
| ------------------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| 2nd                 | Small or Medium | Humanoid or Undead                      |
| 6th                 | —               | Beast, Fey, or Monstrosity              |
| 11th                | Large           | Aberration, Dragon, Elemental, or Giant |
| 17th                | —               | Celestial or Fiend                      |

You can use only the types and sizes available at your level.

### Stitchwork Minion

_Variable size, Undead_

| Statistic            | Value                                                                           |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Armor Class          | 10 + PB (natural armor)                                                         |
| Hit Points           | 2 + your Intelligence modifier + five times your thanatomancer level            |
| Hit Dice             | A number of d6s, d8s, or d10s (based on size) equal to your thanatomancer level |
| Speed                | 30 ft.                                                                          |
| Saving Throws        | Constitution +1 + PB; Wisdom + PB                                               |
| Damage Resistances   | Poison                                                                          |
| Condition Immunities | Exhaustion, poisoned                                                            |
| Senses               | Darkvision 60 ft.; passive Perception 10 + PB                                   |
| Languages            | Understands the languages you speak                                             |
| Proficiency Bonus    | Equals your PB                                                                  |

**Magic Weapons.** The minion's weapon attacks are magical.  
**Unusual Nature.** The minion doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

**Ability scores:** STR 14 (+2), DEX 12 (+1), CON 13 (+1), INT 3 (−4), WIS 10 (+0), CHA 5 (−3)

#### Actions

**Unarmed Strike.** _Melee Weapon Attack:_ your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. _Hit:_ 1d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage (your choice when crafting) + PB necrotic damage.

### Minion grafts

Each grafted body part grants an improvement or trait reflecting its source creature. Harvesting and grafting are separate procedures.

#### Harvesting parts

You can harvest a body part only from creature types and sizes from which you can craft stitchwork minions. You can harvest an arm, leg, wings, tail, or head. Spend 1 minute using leatherworker's tools to separate the part from the corpse and infuse it with energy from the Mortis Veil. Then make an Intelligence (Arcana) or Wisdom (Medicine) check with a DC equal to 10 + the creature's CR (rounded up). On a success, you retrieve a usable body part.

Once you harvest a usable part, that corpse can't be used again for any other purpose: you can't craft a stitchwork minion from it, raise it with _animate dead_, or harvest additional parts. The corpse is completely expended.

#### Grafting parts

You can graft a harvested part onto a stitchwork minion of the same size or one size smaller. The maximum number of grafts per minion is determined by Fleshweaving.

Arms, legs, and heads are limited by the anatomy of the corpse used to create the minion. For example, a Humanoid-corpse minion can have up to two arms, two legs, and one head; a Fiend that originally had four arms can provide up to four arms, and an ettin can provide two heads. If the original corpse had fewer limbs, such as a serpentine creature with no legs, the minion inherits that anatomy for grafting purposes. The GM determines these limits.

Tails and wings are exceptions to the graft limit. You can graft a new tail and a pair of wings onto any minion, regardless of the corpse's original anatomy, and they don't count toward its total grafts. The source creature must be the same size as the minion or one size larger. A successfully grafted tail or pair of wings grants the minion the corresponding trait:

- **Tail.** As a bonus action, the minion can make a melee weapon attack with its tail, using your spell attack modifier to hit, with a reach of 10 feet. On a hit, it deals 1d8 + PB bludgeoning damage.
- **Wings.** The minion has a flying speed equal to its walking speed.

To graft a body part, spend 10 minutes using leatherworker's tools and energy from the Mortis Veil to integrate it. Then make an Intelligence (Arcana) or Wisdom (Medicine) check with a DC equal to 10 + half the harvested creature's CR (rounded up). You have advantage if the part is from the same creature type as the minion's original type. If the part comes from a creature with a lower CR than the minion's original body, subtract the difference between their CRs (rounded down, maximum −5) from the check.

On a failed check, you can immediately expend a spell slot to add a bonus to the roll equal to the spell slot's level. The bonus must be enough to turn the failure into a success, and you can use this bonus only once per minion. If grafting is done during a short or long rest, expend the spell slot at the end of the rest. Otherwise, the part doesn't graft but remains viable for one more attempt. After two failed attempts, it is destroyed. A successful graft grants a trait from the table. A grafted part can't be reused.

#### Minion graft traits

| Creature Type | Arm                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Leg                                                                                                                                             | Head                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Aberration    | **Tentacle Slam.** _Melee Weapon Attack:_ your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. _Hit:_ 1d6 bludgeoning + 2 × PB psychic damage; a creature hit must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be grappled.                                                                                                                                            | **Spider Climb.** The minion can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without an ability check.                         | **Alien Awareness.** The minion can see invisible creatures within 30 ft. and is immune to psychic damage.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Beast         | **Rending Claw.** _Melee Weapon Attack:_ your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. _Hit:_ 1d6 slashing + 2 × PB slashing damage; the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be knocked prone.                                                                                                                                               | **Swift Legs.** The minion's walking speed increases by 10 ft., and it gains a climbing speed equal to its walking speed.                       | **Keen Senses.** The minion has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and can't be surprised.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Celestial     | **Radiant Strike.** _Melee Weapon Attack:_ your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. _Hit:_ 1d6 piercing + 2 × PB radiant damage; the target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC or be outlined in divine light until the end of its next turn. Attack rolls against an outlined target have advantage, and it can't benefit from being invisible. | **Radiant Retreat.** Opportunity attacks against the minion have disadvantage.                                                                  | **Holy Light.** As a bonus action, the minion activates or deactivates bright light in a 30-foot radius. A hostile Undead that starts its turn in the light must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or be blinded until the start of its next turn.                                           |
| Dragon        | **Draconic Claw.** _Melee Weapon Attack:_ your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. _Hit:_ 1d6 slashing + 2 × PB damage of a type matching the dragon's breath weapon.                                                                                                                                                                                                            | **Leaping Charge.** The minion's long and high jump distances are doubled, and it has advantage on Dexterity checks and saving throws.          | **Breath Weapon (1/Day).** The minion exhales elemental energy in a 15-foot cone or 30-foot line (choose when grafting). Each creature in the area makes a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 2 × PB damage of a type matching the dragon's breath weapon on a failure, or half as much on a success. |
| Elemental     | **Elemental Strike.** _Melee Weapon Attack:_ your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. _Hit:_ 3 × PB elemental damage of a type selected from the body part when grafting: acid, cold, fire, or lightning.                                                                                                                                                                        | **Unstoppable.** The minion has advantage on ability checks and saving throws against being grappled or restrained.                             | **Elemental Awareness.** The minion can see in magical darkness out to 30 ft.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Fey           | **Fey Strike.** _Melee Weapon Attack:_ your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. _Hit:_ 1d6 slashing + 2 × PB psychic damage; a creature hit must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or can't take reactions until the end of its next turn.                                                                                                             | **Fey Agility.** The minion's speed increases by 10 ft., and it has advantage on Dexterity saving throws.                                       | **Fey Mind.** The minion has advantage on Charisma saving throws and is immune to being magically put to sleep.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Fiend         | **Infernal Strike.** _Melee Weapon Attack:_ your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. _Hit:_ 1d6 piercing + 2 × PB fire or necrotic damage (choose when grafting).                                                                                                                                                                                                                | **Demonic Stride.** The minion has resistance to fire damage and ignores difficult terrain.                                                     | **Aura of Despair.** Hostile creatures within 10 ft. of the minion have disadvantage on saving throws against being frightened.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Giant         | **Crushing Blow.** _Melee Weapon Attack:_ your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. _Hit:_ 3 × PB bludgeoning damage; a creature hit must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be knocked prone.                                                                                                                                                      | **Titanic Stride.** The minion's carrying capacity is doubled, and it has advantage on Strength checks to shove or grapple.                     | **Keen Eye.** The minion has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and proficiency in Intimidation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Humanoid      | **Precision Grip.** The first time the minion makes a weapon attack on its turn, it can add your Intelligence modifier to its attack and damage rolls.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | **Nimble Step.** The minion has proficiency in Stealth and advantage on ability checks and saving throws to avoid being grappled or restrained. | **Tactical Mind.** The minion gains proficiency in Intelligence and Wisdom saving throws and can take the Help action as a bonus action.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Monstrosity   | **Savage Bite.** _Melee Weapon Attack:_ your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. _Hit:_ 1d6 piercing + PB poison damage; a creature hit is poisoned until the end of its next turn.                                                                                                                                                                                              | **Climber's Form.** The minion gains a climbing speed equal to its walking speed.                                                               | **Hunter's Senses.** The minion is immune to being frightened and has advantage on attack rolls against creatures with fewer than half their hit points remaining.                                                                                                                                                           |
| Undead        | **Paralytic Claw.** _Melee Weapon Attack:_ your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. _Hit:_ 1d6 slashing + 2 × PB necrotic damage; a creature hit must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or have its speed halved until the end of its next turn.                                                                                                     | **Relentless March.** The minion is immune to being knocked prone and ignores difficult terrain.                                                | **Eyes of Death (1/Day).** The minion gazes at a creature it can see within 30 ft. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or become frightened until the end of its next turn.                                                                                                        |
