frontmatter.summary: Endures enemy attacks and protects allies with necromantic power

entries.body:
# Path of the Graveguard

Graveguards turn the power of death inward, becoming enduring defenders who drain vitality from those who challenge them.

## Tool Proficiency

_3rd-level Path of the Graveguard feature_

You gain proficiency with smith's tools. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of artisan's tools of your choice.

## Death's Bulwark

_3rd-level Path of the Graveguard feature_

You gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons.

While wearing medium armor or wielding a shield, when you make a saving throw against a spell or magical effect, you can expend 1 mortis point to add your Intelligence modifier (minimum +1) to the roll.

**Grave Binding.** The first time on your turn when you deal necrotic damage to a Large or smaller creature with a cantrip or melee weapon attack, you can force it to succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC = 8 + your Intelligence modifier + your proficiency bonus) or have its speed reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn.

## Grim Vitality

_3rd-level Path of the Graveguard feature_

Whenever you deal damage to a creature with a melee weapon attack or deal necrotic damage with a spell or feature that targets only one creature, you gain temporary hit points equal to the damage dealt. These temporary hit points last until the start of your next turn.

## Warden's Intervention

_6th-level Path of the Graveguard feature_

You gain the following benefits:

**Veil of Retaliation.** When a hostile creature hits an ally within 30 feet of you with an attack, you can use your reaction to expend 1 mortis point and immediately use a Veil Technique that uses a reaction, targeting the attacker as if the technique came from the ally. You must still spend the technique's normal mortis point cost.

**Warding Aegis.** As a reaction when an ally within 15 feet of you is targeted by an attack, expend 2 mortis points to teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the attacker. The attack targets you instead. Until the end of the attacker's turn, you gain a bonus to AC equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum +1) against that attacker. At 13th level, you can instead expend 3 mortis points to use this feature to assist an ally within 30 feet of you.

## Sentinel of the Veil

_10th-level Path of the Graveguard feature_

As a bonus action, expend 2 mortis points to tether a creature you can see within 10 feet of you with deathly energy for 1 minute. If the tethered creature moves more than 10 feet away from you, it takes necrotic damage equal to twice your Intelligence modifier + your proficiency bonus. You can also force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your Intelligence modifier + your proficiency bonus). On a failed save, it is pulled up to 10 feet toward you and knocked prone.

## Deathless Bastion

_18th-level Path of the Graveguard feature_

You have advantage on ability checks and saving throws against the grappled, paralyzed, prone, and stunned conditions. You can't be forcibly moved against your will.

**Eternal Warden.** As a reaction when an ally within 30 feet of you would drop to 0 hit points, expend 5 mortis points or a 5th-level or higher spell slot to cause the ally to drop to 1 hit point instead. Once you use this reaction, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

_From Erevan's Guide to Death & Beyond._

entries.title: Path of the Reaper
entries.summary: Chains swift weapon strikes and cuts at the soul

frontmatter.title: Path of the Reaper
frontmatter.summary: Chains swift weapon strikes and cuts at the soul

entries.body:
# Path of the Reaper

Reapers slip through shadows and the Mortis Veil, delivering swift, precise strikes that leave little warning before death arrives.

## Tool Proficiency

_3rd-level Path of the Reaper feature_

You gain proficiency with alchemist's supplies. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of artisan's tools of your choice.

## Chained Strikes

_3rd-level Path of the Reaper feature_

When you use your action to target a creature with a melee weapon attack or melee spell attack and miss, you can use your bonus action to make a melee weapon attack against the same target.

When you use your action to target a creature with a melee weapon attack or melee spell attack and hit, you can make a melee weapon attack against the same target as part of the same action, or expend 1 mortis point to unleash a chained strike. As part of the chained strike, teleport up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space within reach of a different hostile creature you can see, then make one melee weapon attack against it as part of the same action. A creature can't be targeted more than once in a chained strike each turn. You can use this feature only once per turn.

At 10th level, after you hit with a chained strike, you can expend 1 additional mortis point to teleport to a third target and make another melee weapon attack. At 18th level, you can expend 1 additional mortis point to teleport to a fourth target and attack it in the same way.

## Reaper's Weaponry

_3rd-level Path of the Reaper feature_

- You can use your Intelligence modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity for attack and damage rolls with melee weapons you are proficient with.
- The first time you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack on your turn, the attack deals extra necrotic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1).

## Veilpiercer

_6th-level Path of the Reaper feature_

**Necrotic Strikes.** Your necrotic damage from Reaper's Weaponry ignores resistance, and immunity to necrotic damage is treated as resistance instead.

**Severing Rhythm.** When you use your action to cast a cantrip, you can expend 1 mortis point to make a melee weapon attack as a bonus action.

## Mortis Strike

_10th-level Path of the Reaper feature_

When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack as part of Chained Strikes, you can use a Veil Technique that triggers on a hit with a weapon attack, even if you have already used one. You must still pay the technique's mortis point cost.

## Death's Final Cut

_18th-level Path of the Reaper feature_

You gain the following benefits:

**Soul Conversion.** When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack or melee spell attack, you can expend a spell slot of 1st to 5th level to regain mortis points equal to twice the spell slot's level. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

**Soul Severance.** When you hit a creature with half its hit points or fewer remaining with a melee weapon attack or melee spell attack, you can expend 5 mortis points to attempt a soul-rending strike. The target must make a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your Intelligence modifier + your proficiency bonus). On a failed save, it takes 6d10 necrotic damage, can't regain hit points until the end of your next turn, and has disadvantage on saving throws against your spells for the same duration. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and suffers no additional effects. This damage ignores resistance and immunity to necrotic damage.

_From Erevan's Guide to Death & Beyond._

entries.title: Archangel
entries.summary: Otherworldly Patron for the Warlock

frontmatter.title: Archangel
frontmatter.summary: Otherworldly Patron for the Warlock

entries.body:
You made a pact with an archangel, one of the highest-ranking members of heaven. Archangels can be peaceful entities that aim to heal others' wounds, or they may be burning with wrath and a need for heavenly justice. You serve as the archangel's hand, watching over the world, observing mortals, and reporting and even punishing the sinful.

In return, the archangel provides you with special gifts. You may have acquired this pact as a member of a temple dedicated to the forces of good, or after you were saved from a dire situation by the archangel who saw a potential in you for greatness.

## Expanded Spell List

The archangel lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

## Archangel expanded spells

| Spell level | Spells                                        |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| 1st         | [[Bless]], [[Cure Wounds]]                    |
| 2nd         | [[Angelic Executioner]], [[Spiritual Weapon]] |
| 3rd         | [[Beacon of Hope]], [[Revivify]]              |
| 4th         | [[Dictate Morality]], [[Radiant Storm]]       |
| 5th         | [[Burden of Sins]], well of blessing          |

## Features

> [!info]- Carrier of an Angelic Spirit (level 1)
> At 1st level, you become an accepted member of the angelic courts of heaven. You learn Celestial and can telepathically communicate with celestials within 60 feet of you.

> [!info]- Aid of Angels (level 1)
> Starting at 1st level, you gain the ability to magically summon a celestial that can destroy your enemies and heal your allies. As a bonus action, you summon a Medium celestial at an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet of you. The summoned celestial remains for 1 minute or until you use this feature to summon another one.
>
> When you summon the celestial, it can make a melee spell attack against a creature within 5 feet of it using your statistics or heal a creature within 5 feet of it. If it attacks, the target takes 1d6 fire or radiant damage (one of your choice) on a hit. If it heals, the target regains 1d6 hit points. When you reach 10th level, the damage and the amount of hit points regained increases to 2d6.
>
> As a bonus action on your turn, you can command the celestial to move up to 30 feet and make it attack or heal again.
>
> You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

> [!info]- Channeling Angelic Powers (level 6)
> Starting at 6th level, you can channel angelic powers. When you deal damage with a spell or another magical effect, you can use your reaction to change the damage type to radiant. If the celestial you summoned with the Aid of Angels feature is within 30 feet of one of the targets of the magical effect when you use this feature, the effect deals an extra 1d6 fire or radiant damage (one of your choice).

> [!info]- Angelic Protection (level 10)
> At 10th level, angelic powers watch over you themselves. Under their watchful eye, you gain resistance to radiant damage.
>
> Additionally, you can use a bonus action to gain resistance to necrotic damage for 1 minute. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest to use it again.

> [!info]- Angelic Intervention (level 14)
> Starting at 14th level, you gain the ability to call angelic forces to your aid. As an action, you choose a point within 30 feet of you. A troop of angelic figures rushes forth in a direction you choose starting at that point, harming the enemies in a 15-foot cone, and healing the allies within the area.
>
> Enemies in the cone must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 4d10 fire or radiant damage (one of your choice) and is blinded until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, the damage is halved and the creature is not blinded. Allies within the cone regain 2d10 hit points.
>
> Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest to use it again.

_From Corpus Angelus._

frontmatter.summary: Otherworldly Patron that grants alternate Warlock Patron magic

entries.body:
You have entered a Pact with a powerful entity of the faerie. Whether you were gifted this Pact or tricked your Patron into granting you power, you draw upon the whimsical and terrifying magic of the Fey. Only the eldest Archfey, ancient sylvan spirits, and the most powerful coven leaders can form such Pacts.

## Patron Magic

You can choose for your Eldritch Blast to deal Psychic damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier instead of Force damage.

You also learn the spells in the following table at the Warlock levels shown. They count as Warlock spells for you, do not count against Spells Known, and cannot be replaced.

| Warlock Level | Spells                                              |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| 2nd           | [[Faerie Fire]], [[Sleep]]                          |
| 3rd           | [[Misty Step]], Phantasmal Force                    |
| 5th           | [[Fear]], [[Hypnotic Pattern]]                      |
| 7th           | [[Hallucinatory Terrain]], [[Greater Invisibility]] |
| 9th           | [[Mislead]], [[Seeming]]                            |

## Fey Presence

_2nd-level Archfey Patron feature_

You can beguile others with fey magic. As an action, choose one creature that can see or hear you within 10 feet; it must make a Wisdom saving throw or be Charmed or Frightened, as you choose, for 10 minutes. The effect ends early if the creature takes damage or you or an ally forces it to make a saving throw. You can use this feature once between rests. Afterwards, you must expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use it again.

## Beguiling Blast

_6th-level Archfey Patron feature_

When you deal Psychic damage to a creature with Eldritch Blast, it has disadvantage on the first attack roll it makes before the start of your next turn. Creatures immune to the Charmed condition are immune to this effect.

## Misty Escape

_6th-level Archfey Patron feature_

When you take damage, you can use your reaction to turn Invisible and teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet. You remain Invisible until the start of your next turn or until you attack, cast a spell, or force a saving throw. You can use this once between rests, then must expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use it again.

## Whimsical Defense

_10th-level Archfey Patron feature_

You gain Immunity to the Charmed condition. When a creature attempts to inflict the Charmed condition on you, it makes a Wisdom saving throw; on a failure, it suffers the effects of Fey Presence. If it is also immune to Charmed, it takes Psychic damage equal to your Warlock level.

## Terrible Delights

_14th-level Archfey Patron feature_

Your Warlock spells and features ignore immunity to the Charmed condition, though creatures affected by them have advantage on saving throws. When a creature fails its saving throw against Fey Presence, you can plunge it into a concentrated illusion of emotion. It perceives only itself, you, and that reality; repeated damage grants Wisdom saving throws. Success grants immunity to this enhanced effect for 24 hours.

---

frontmatter.summary: Otherworldly Patron that grants alternate Warlock Patron magic
frontmatter.incomplete_reason: Mechanics were transcribed from the supplied Alternate Warlock source and require line-by-line verification before use.

entries.body:
You have entered into a Pact with a sinister ruler of the Shadowfell, imprisoned within a Domain of Dread and able to affect the outside world only through trusted servants. Your Darklord grants you a fraction of its umbral power.

## Patron Magic

You can choose for Eldritch Blast to deal Necrotic damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

You also learn the spells in the following table at the Warlock levels shown. They count as Warlock spells for you, do not count against Spells Known, and cannot be replaced.

| Warlock Level | Spells                                |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| 2nd           | Hex, [[Inflict Wounds]]               |
| 3rd           | [[Blindness-Deafness]], [[Blur]]      |
| 5th           | [[Fear]], Enemies Abound              |
| 7th           | Accursed Touch, [[Phantasmal Killer]] |
| 9th           | [[Dream]], Enervation                 |

## Fell Curses

_2nd-level Darklord Patron feature_

Your concentration on Darklord Magic spells cannot be broken by taking damage. Attack rolls against a creature under a Darklord Magic spell score a critical hit on a d20 roll of 19 or 20. When you deal Necrotic damage to such a creature, you gain temporary hit points equal to half the damage, up to your Warlock level.

## Shadow Warrior

_2nd-level Darklord Patron feature_

You learn [[Armor of Shadows]] even if you do not meet its prerequisites, and this Invocation cannot be replaced. While Armor of Shadows is active, add your Pact modifier to Stealth checks made in dim light or darkness.

## Cursed Specter

_6th-level Darklord Patron feature_

When a Humanoid under a Darklord Magic spell dies, you can capture its spirit as a reaction. You can have one spirit at a time. As an action, consume it to summon a Specter at an unoccupied space within 10 feet. It uses your spell save DC and spell attack modifier, acts on your turn, and remains for 1 minute unless destroyed or you become Unconscious.

## Dread Mantle

_10th-level Darklord Patron feature_

When a creature under a Darklord Magic spell damages you, reduce the damage by your Pact modifier, minimum 1. You also add your Pact modifier, minimum +1, to death saving throws.

## Right Hand of Dread

_14th-level Darklord Patron feature_

When a creature under a Darklord Magic spell is slain, use your reaction to regain one expended Pact Magic spell slot instead of capturing it with Cursed Specter. You may expend a spell slot when using Cursed Specter to conjure a Specter directly; only one Specter can be conjured this way at a time.

---

entries.title: Deep One
entries.summary: Otherworldly Patron that grants alternate Warlock Patron magic

frontmatter.title: Deep One
frontmatter.summary: Otherworldly Patron that grants alternate Warlock Patron magic

entries.body:
You have bonded yourself to a primordial force of the ancient waters. Deep Ones are thalassic entities whose unknown motives stretch back to an age before recorded history. Their servants wield the crushing, alien pressure of the ocean depths.

## Patron Magic

Your Eldritch Blast can deal Cold damage instead of Force damage, equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

You also learn the spells in the following table at the Warlock levels shown. They count as Warlock spells for you, do not count against Spells Known, and cannot be replaced.

| Warlock Level | Spells                                |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| 2nd           | Create Water, Torrent                 |
| 3rd           | Aura of Frost, [[Gust of Wind]]       |
| 5th           | Tidal Wave, [[Sleet Storm]]           |
| 7th           | [[Control Water]], Eldritch Tentacles |
| 9th           | [[Cone of Cold]], Maelstrom           |

## Grasp of the Deep

_2nd-level Deep One Patron feature_

Whenever you deal Cold damage to a Large or smaller creature, you can conjure a spectral tendril from your Patron in that creature's space. The creature is Grappled by the tendril for 1 minute.

As an action, a grappled creature can make a Strength check against your spell save DC. On a success, the grapple ends and the tendril disappears.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Pact modifier (minimum of once). You regain all uses when you finish a long rest. If you have no uses remaining, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use it again.

## Scion of the Deep

_2nd-level Deep One Patron feature_

Your Pact alters your physiology so you can survive the depths. You gain Resistance to Cold damage, a swimming speed of 30 feet, and the ability to breathe air and water.

While underwater, you and another creature underwater can understand each other as if you shared a common language.

## Oceanic Grasp

_6th-level Deep One Patron feature_

If you deal Cold damage to a creature with Eldritch Blast two or more times in one turn, you can use Grasp of the Deep without expending a use of that feature.

## Greater Tendrils

_10th-level Deep One Patron feature_

You can use Grasp of the Deep on Huge creatures. When a creature begins its turn Grappled by Grasp of the Deep, it takes 2d8 Cold damage.

## Thalassic Mind

_10th-level Deep One Patron feature_

Your concentration on Deep Magic spells cannot be broken by taking damage.

## Unleash the Depths

_14th-level Deep One Patron feature_

As an action, you conjure up to five Grasp of the Deep tendrils in spaces of your choice within 30 feet of you. Each tendril forces one creature within 10 feet to make a Dexterity saving throw.

On a failed save, the creature takes 2d8 Cold damage and is Restrained by the tendril for its duration. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and is not Restrained.

You can use this feature once per long rest without a cost. After that, you must spend a Pact Magic spell slot to use it again.

---

entries.body:
You have entered a Pact with a powerful Celestial native to the Upper Planes. Whether your Patron sought you as an ally or you proved yourself worthy, your pact carries the responsibility of supporting good and opposing evil.

## Patron Magic

You can choose for Eldritch Blast to deal Radiant damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

You also learn the spells in the following table at the Warlock levels shown. They count as Warlock spells for you, do not count against Spells Known, and cannot be replaced.

| Warlock Level | Spells                                  |

| 2nd           | [[Cure Wounds]], [[Guiding Bolt]]       |

| 5th           | [[Daylight]], [[Revivify]]              |
| 7th           | [[Guardian of Faith]], [[Wall of Fire]] |
| 9th           | Conjure Celestial, [[Flame Strike]]     |

## Celestial Light

_2nd-level Exalted Patron feature_

As a bonus action, choose one of your hands to shed bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for another 20 feet. You can use Celestial Light once between rests at no cost, or expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use it again. You can restore hit points using this feature as described in the source.

## Exalted Magic

_2nd-level Exalted Patron feature_

You gain the listed Exalted Patron spells. They count as Warlock spells for you, do not count against Spells Known, and cannot be replaced.

## Radiant Conduit

_6th-level Exalted Patron feature_

You gain Resistance to Radiant damage. While Celestial Light is active, you can expend additional uses to restore extra hit points and gain restorative benefits against conditions as specified by the source.

## Celestial Fortitude

_10th-level Exalted Patron feature_

You gain temporary hit points equal to your Warlock level after finishing a long rest and cannot be reduced below 1 hit point by Radiant damage while Celestial Light is active.

## Blinding Defiance

_14th-level Exalted Patron feature_

When a creature strikes you with an attack, you can reveal its location with holy light and force it to make a Constitution saving throw or be Blinded until the end of its next turn.

entries.title: Fiend
entries.summary: Otherworldly Patron that channels infernal flame and vitality from death

frontmatter.title: Fiend
frontmatter.summary: Otherworldly Patron that channels infernal flame and vitality from death

entries.body:
_2nd-level Otherworldly Patron feature_

You have entered a Pact with a powerful Fiend from the lower planes. Whether you struck a bargain, were coerced, or tricked your Patron, you are now linked to a being of absolute evil. Only the most powerful Fiends can serve as Patrons; archdevils, demon lords, and especially mighty servants of extraplanar evil are common.

## Fiendish Magic

Your Patron infuses your magic with infernal flame. You can choose for Eldritch Blast to deal Fire damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier on a hit, ignoring Resistance to Fire damage.

You also learn the spells in the following table at the Warlock levels shown. They count as Warlock spells for you but do not count against your Spells Known, and you cannot replace them.

| Warlock Level | Spells                             |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| 2nd           | [[Command]], [[Hellish Rebuke]]    |
| 3rd           | [[Blindness-Deafness]], Flame Whip |
| 5th           | [[Bestow Curse]], [[Fireball]]     |
| 7th           | [[Blight]], [[Wall of Fire]]       |
| 9th           | [[Cloudkill]], Immolation          |

## Dark Vitality

_2nd-level Fiend Patron feature_

You draw vitality from death and pain. Whenever you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Warlock level + your Pact modifier. You can also use this feature as a reaction when a hostile creature within 10 feet of you is reduced to 0 hit points.

## Accursed Flames

_6th-level Fiend Patron feature_

Your magic scours the souls of your foes. Whenever you deal Fire damage to a creature, it cannot regain hit points or gain temporary hit points until the start of your next turn.

## Dark Bargain

_6th-level Fiend Patron feature_

You sacrifice your vitality to alter fate. When you fail an ability check or saving throw, roll a d10 and add the result to your roll, reducing your hit point maximum by the same amount. This reduction is restored at the end of your next long rest.

## Fiendish Resilience

_10th-level Fiend Patron feature_

At the end of each short or long rest, choose one damage type. You gain Resistance to that type until the end of your next short or long rest. Damage you take from magical or silvered weapons ignores this Resistance.

## Hurl Into Hell

_14th-level Fiend Patron feature_

When you deal damage to a creature with Eldritch Blast, you can banish it to your Patron's domain until the end of your next turn. When it returns to the space it left or the nearest unoccupied space, it takes 6d10 Psychic damage if it is not a Fiend.

Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before using it again.

---

You made a Pact with an incomprehensible entity from beyond your reality, such as a Far Realm intelligence or an ancient void between stars. Its secrets bend minds and expose truths mortals were never meant to understand.

## Patron Magic

You can choose for Eldritch Blast to deal Psychic damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

You also learn the spells in the following table at the Warlock levels shown. They count as Warlock spells for you, do not count against Spells Known, and cannot be replaced.

| 7th           | [[Confusion]], Eldritch Tentacles  |

## Awakened Mind

_2nd-level Great Old One Patron feature_

You can telepathically communicate with any creature you can see within 60 feet. You do not need to share a language, but it must know at least one language. You may communicate with only one creature at a time. You also gain Resistance to Psychic damage.

## Mental Lance

_6th-level Great Old One Patron feature_

You gain a lance-shaped psionic strike that deals Psychic damage and leaves the target Disoriented or Stunned depending on its failed saving throw.

## Psionic Ward

_10th-level Great Old One Patron feature_

When you finish a short or long rest, choose a psychic resistance or mental defense granted by your entity. Your ward gives you advantage against mind-reading, fear, and charm effects until the next rest.

## Thought Shield

_10th-level Great Old One Patron feature_

Your mind cannot be read except by explicit consent. Creatures that attempt to read your thoughts take Psychic damage and you gain Resistance to Psychic damage.

## Create Thrall

_14th-level Great Old One Patron feature_

You gain control over a creature reduced by your magic to 0 hit points. It becomes a Thrall until dispelled or destroyed and acts under your command.

frontmatter.title: Nature
frontmatter.summary: Otherworldly Patron that grants alternate Warlock Patron magic

entries.body:
You have entered into a Pact with a primordial force of the wild. Mortals seek these powers out: they climb to the peaks, wade into the black water of old swamps, and wait under great storms until something answers. What answers asks one thing of you: to stand guard over the wild against the evil that would turn it into a battlefield. Only the oldest powers of the natural world can form such Pacts. Living mountains, the spirits of ancient swamps, and the storms that circle the high sky are most common.

## Primordial Magic

_2nd-level Nature Patron feature_

Your Patron infuses your magic with the power of the wild. Choose an Aspect from the table below. Once chosen, your Aspect cannot be changed. You can choose for your Eldritch Blast beams to deal your Aspect's damage type, equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier on hit.

| Aspect   | Embodies            | Damage    |
| -------- | ------------------- | --------- |
| Mountain | Stone and avalanche | Thunder   |
| Swamp    | Rot and reeds       | Poison    |
| Sky      | Storm and wind      | Lightning |

You also learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They are Warlock spells for you, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced:

| Warlock Level | Spells                                     |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| 2nd           | [[Entangle]], [[Fog Cloud]]                |
| 3rd           | [[Gust of Wind]], [[Spike Growth]]         |
| 5th           | [[Meld Into Stone]], [[Water Breathing]]   |
| 7th           | [[Control Water]], [[Freedom of Movement]] |
| 9th           | [[Commune With Nature]], [[Tree Stride]]   |

## Child of the Wild

_2nd-level Nature Patron feature_

Your Pact has taken root in your body. You gain Resistance to your Aspect's damage type, and nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement.

## Rooted Blast

_6th-level Nature Patron feature_

Your Patron's power seizes your foes' footing. Once per turn, when you deal your Aspect's damage to a Large or smaller creature with Eldritch Blast, you can force it to make a Strength saving throw, expending one use of this feature. On a failure, roots, stone, or reeds hold its feet, and its speed is 0 until the end of its next turn.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Pact modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. If you have no uses left, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use this feature again.

## Primordial Form

_10th-level Nature Patron feature_

You can take the shape of the wild force behind your Aspect. As a bonus action, you assume this form for 1 minute. Your skin hardens into stone plates, a hide of wet bark and reeds, or a crackling skin of storm cloud, matching your Aspect. While transformed:

- When you transform, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Warlock level + your Pact modifier (minimum of 1).
- Damage you take from weapon attacks is reduced by your Pact modifier (minimum of 1).

You can end this form early with a bonus action. You can transform once in between each short or long rest at no cost. After that, you must expend a Pact Magic spell slot to transform again.

## Wrath of the Wild

_14th-level Nature Patron feature_

You call down the full fury of your Patron. As an action, choose a point within 60 feet. Each creature in a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 6d10 damage of your Aspect's type, and if it is Large or smaller, roots, stone, or reeds hold its feet, and its speed is 0 until the end of its next turn. On a success, it takes half as much damage and suffers no other effect.

You can use this feature once per long rest at no cost. After that, you must expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use it again.

---

entries.title: Noble Genie
entries.summary: Otherworldly Patron that grants alternate Warlock Patron magic

frontmatter.title: Noble Genie
frontmatter.summary: Otherworldly Patron that grants alternate Warlock Patron magic

entries.body:
You entered a Pact with a Noble Genie, ruler of one of the elemental planes. Only the most powerful dao, djinn, efreeti, and marids can grant such Pacts. Noble Genies are bound by bargains, grandeur, and ancient elemental law.

## Choose Your Noble Genie

Choose Dao, Djinn, Efreeti, or Marid. Your choice determines the Element and damage type associated with your Patron.

| Noble Genie | Element | Damage Type |
| ----------- | ------- | ----------- |
| Dao         | Earth   | Bludgeoning |
| Djinn       | Air     | Thunder     |
| Efreeti     | Fire    | Fire        |
| Marid       | Water   | Cold        |

## Magic Vessel

_2nd-level Noble Genie Patron feature_

Your Patron gifts you a magic Vessel as a sign of your Pact. It appears as a Tiny container of your choice. It has hit points equal to twice your Warlock level and an Armor Class equal to your spell save DC. If it is lost or destroyed, it reappears next to you at the end of your next long rest. The Vessel can serve as a Trinket for one of your Eldritch Invocations.

Inside the Vessel is a 20-foot cube extradimensional space. As an action, you can hold a Medium or smaller object to its opening and store it inside. As an action, you can touch your Vessel and enter this space. You can remain inside for a number of hours equal to half your Warlock level.

You exit early by using an action or if the Vessel is destroyed. Whenever you exit, you can bring objects out of the space with you, and you appear in the Vessel’s space.

## Noble Magic

_2nd-level Noble Genie Patron feature_

Your Patron infuses your magic with its power. You can choose for Eldritch Blast to deal the damage type of your Noble Genie's Element equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

You learn the spells in the following table at the Warlock levels shown. They count as Warlock spells for you, do not count against Spells Known, and cannot be replaced.

| Warlock Level | Spells                               |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| 2nd           | [[Sleep]], your Genie spell          |
| 3rd           | [[Enlarge-Reduce]], your Genie spell |
| 5th           | [[Fly]], your Genie spell            |
| 7th           | Polymorph, your Genie spell          |
| 9th           | [[Arcane Hand]], your Genie spell    |

The first spell shown at each level is granted by every Noble Genie. Your choice of Dao, Djinn, Efreeti, or Marid determines the second spell.

| Warlock Level | Dao Spells        | Djinn Spells             | Efreeti Spells     | Marid Spells     |
| ------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------ | ---------------- |
| 2nd           | [[Sanctuary]]     | Thunderwave              | [[Burning Hands]]  | Torrent          |
| 3rd           | Spike Growth      | [[Gust of Wind]]         | [[Flaming Sphere]] | [[Misty Step]]   |
| 5th           | Meld into Stone   | [[Gaseous Form]]         | Minute Meteors     | Tidal Wave       |
| 7th           | Pillars of Earth  | [[Greater Invisibility]] | [[Fire Shield]]    | Watery Sphere    |
| 9th           | [[Wall of Stone]] | [[Seeming]]              | [[Flame Strike]]   | [[Cone of Cold]] |

## Ethereal Nature

_6th-level Noble Genie Patron feature_

Your elemental nature begins to physically change you. You gain Resistance to damage of your Noble Genie’s Element.

Once per turn, when you deal Element damage with Eldritch Blast, you can force the target to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the target instantly switches places with you.

## Mystical Sanctuary

_10th-level Noble Genie Patron feature_

When you enter your Vessel, you can choose up to five willing creatures within 30 feet to enter with you. These creatures can remain inside for up to 1 hour, but they exit early if you leave, the Vessel is destroyed, or you use an action to eject them.

While inside the Vessel, creatures can complete a short rest in 10 minutes, following the normal limitations of short rests.

## Limited Wish

_14th-level Noble Genie Patron feature_

As an action, you can hold aloft your Vessel to cast one spell of 6th level or lower from any spell list. The spell must have a casting time of one action or one bonus action. Your Vessel replaces material components, including components with a gold cost.

Once you use this feature, you must finish three long rests before using it again.

---

entries.title: The Returned
entries.summary: Otherworldly Patron that grants alternate Warlock Patron magic

frontmatter.title: The Returned
frontmatter.summary: Otherworldly Patron that grants alternate Warlock Patron magic

entries.body:
You remember the dying: cold creeping up from your fingertips, the room's sounds draining away, and then a hand that wasn't there closing around your spirit. Maybe you led a life of good deeds with a part still to play, or carried a potential you never knew about, or lived in sin with no idea what earned the second chance. The angel named its terms, and when you accepted them it fused itself to your body and spirit. The wound that killed you has closed into a seam of light.

## Returned Magic

_2nd-level Returned Patron feature_

Your savior infuses your magic with celestial light. You can choose for your Eldritch Blast beams to deal Radiant damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier on hit.

You also learn certain spells at the Warlock levels below. They are Warlock spells for you, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known, and they cannot be replaced:

| Warlock Level | Spells                                      |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| 2nd           | [[False Life]], [[Bless]]                   |
| 3rd           | [[Find Steed]], [[Zone of Truth]]           |
| 5th           | [[Mass Healing Word]], [[Spirit Guardians]] |
| 7th           | [[Death Ward]], [[Guardian of Faith]]       |
| 9th           | [[Mass Cure Wounds]], [[Raise Dead]]        |

## Angelic Ward

_2nd-level Returned Patron feature_

Your savior stands between you and harm. When you take damage from an attack or effect you can see, you can use your reaction to reduce that damage by an amount equal to your Warlock level + your Pact modifier.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Pact modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. If you have no uses left, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use this feature again.

## Sanctuary

_6th-level Returned Patron feature_

Your savior can pull you back to the place your spirit stood when it found you, a Sanctuary such as a heavenly room or a quiet mountaintop where nothing can harm you. Decide its look with your DM.

As an action, you vanish into your Sanctuary. You can't be targeted or affected by anything until the start of your next turn, when you reappear in the space you left, or the nearest unoccupied space, and regain hit points equal to your Warlock level + your Pact modifier.

You can use this feature once between each short or long rest at no cost. After that, you must expend a Pact Magic spell slot to use it again.

## Angelic Wings

_10th-level Returned Patron feature_

Your savior's wings unfold from your shoulder blades. As a bonus action, you manifest a pair of wings of light for 1 minute. While they are manifested, you have a flying speed equal to your walking speed and can hover, and the wings shed bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet. You can retract them early with a bonus action.

You can manifest your wings once in between each short or long rest at no cost. After that, you must expend a Pact Magic spell slot to manifest them again.

## Grace Beyond Death

_14th-level Returned Patron feature_

The grace that returned you once returns you again. When you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, your savior pulls you back instead. You drop to a number of hit points equal to twice your Warlock level, and light flares from the wound that would have ended you. Once you use this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can use it again.

---

entries.title: Undying
entries.summary: Otherworldly Patron that grants alternate Warlock Patron magic

frontmatter.title: Undying
frontmatter.summary: Otherworldly Patron that grants alternate Warlock Patron magic
frontmatter.incomplete_reason: Mechanics were transcribed from the supplied Alternate Warlock source and require line-by-line verification before use.

entries.body:
You entered a Pact with a formerly mortal creature that found a way to cheat death. The Undying are some of the most ancient undead powers, and their bargains offer survival, resilience, and terrifying longevity.

## Patron Magic

Your Eldritch Blast can deal Necrotic damage equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

You also learn the spells in the following table at the Warlock levels shown. They count as Warlock spells for you, do not count against Spells Known, and cannot be replaced.

| Warlock Level | Spells                                          |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| 2nd           | Cause Fear, Ray of Sickness                     |
| 3rd           | [[Blindness-Deafness]], [[Ray of Enfeeblement]] |
| 5th           | [[Fear]], [[Phantom Steed]]                     |
| 7th           | [[Blight]], [[Death Ward]]                      |
| 9th           | [[Antilife Shell]], [[Contagion]]               |

## Necrotic Husk

_2nd-level Undying Patron feature_

As a bonus action, transform into a Necrotic Husk for 1 minute. While transformed, you resemble your Patron and are Horrifying to look upon; gain temporary hit points equal to your Warlock level; increase your Necrotic damage by your Pact modifier; and gain Resistance to Necrotic damage.

## Touch of the Grave

_2nd-level Undying Patron feature_

You can drain vitality from a creature harmed by your Necrotic spells. On a hit, it cannot regain hit points until the start of your next turn and you gain temporary hit points equal to half the Necrotic damage dealt.

## Lifedrinker

_6th-level Undying Patron feature_

When you deal Necrotic damage with Eldritch Blast, the target also loses a number of hit points equal to your Pact modifier until the end of your next turn.

## Unsettling Visage

_10th-level Undying Patron feature_

You gain Immunity to the Frightened condition, and creatures that see your Necrotic Husk must make a Wisdom saving throw or become Frightened.

## Unnatural Resilience

_10th-level Undying Patron feature_

You gain Resistance to Poison damage and Immunity to disease and the Poisoned condition.

## Unending Life

_14th-level Undying Patron feature_

You can stabilize yourself at 0 hit points once per long rest and return to life if slain by means within the Undying Patron’s source mechanics.

---

entries.title: Wyrm
entries.summary: Otherworldly Patron that grants alternate Warlock Patron magic

frontmatter.title: Wyrm
frontmatter.summary: Otherworldly Patron that grants alternate Warlock Patron magic
frontmatter.incomplete_reason: Mechanics were transcribed from the supplied Alternate Warlock source and require line-by-line verification before use.

entries.body:
Great dragons are innately arcane beings with lifespans beyond mortal comprehension. Kind or terrible, benevolent or malicious, elder dragons make for dangerous Patrons whose motives exceed mortal understanding.

## Patron Magic

You can choose for Eldritch Blast to deal damage matching your Draconic Spark: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison. This damage is equal to 1d10 + your Pact modifier.

You also learn the spells in the following table at the Warlock levels shown. They count as Warlock spells for you, do not count against Spells Known, and cannot be replaced.

| Warlock Level | Spells                                 |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| 2nd           | [[Command]], [[Burning Hands]]         |
| 3rd           | Dragon's Breath, [[Scorching Ray]]     |
| 5th           | [[Fear]], [[Fireball]]                 |
| 7th           | [[Dominate Monster]], [[Wall of Fire]] |
| 9th           | Conjure Dragon, [[Legend Lore]]        |

## Draconic Spark

_2nd-level Wyrm Patron feature_

Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison for your Draconic Spark. You gain Resistance to that damage type; Warlock spells you cast that deal damage can deal your Spark damage instead; you gain Draconic language proficiency; and you learn [[Beguiling Influence]], which cannot be replaced. If you already know it, choose another qualifying Eldritch Invocation.

## Wyrm Magic

_2nd-level Wyrm Patron feature_

You gain the listed Wyrm Patron spells. They count as Warlock spells for you, do not count against Spells Known, and cannot be replaced.

## Draconic Blast

_6th-level Wyrm Patron feature_

When you use Eldritch Blast or cast a Warlock spell dealing Draconic Spark damage, you can produce it from your mouth without a Trinket or focus. Against Resistance, ignore it; treat Immunity as Resistance; and treat rolls of 1 or 2 on Spark damage dice as 3.

## Regal Presence

_10th-level Wyrm Patron feature_

You gain Immunity to the Charmed and Frightened conditions. You can cast Conjure Dragon without material components, and the conjured Dragon’s Essence matches your Draconic Spark.

## Dragon Wings

_14th-level Wyrm Patron feature_

As a bonus action, manifest or retract Draconic Wings. While manifested, you have a flying speed equal to your walking speed. Wings destroy armor or clothing not designed to accommodate them.

## Ancient Blast

_14th-level Wyrm Patron feature_

As an action, exhale elemental power in a 25-foot cone or 50-foot line. Creatures make Dexterity saves, take 6d10 Draconic Spark damage on a failure or half on a success, and suffer the additional effects of Eldritch Blast only on a failure. You can use this once per long rest, or expend a Pact Magic spell slot afterward.

---

entries.title: Celestial Summoner
entries.summary: Arcane Tradition for the Wizard

frontmatter.title: Celestial Summoner
frontmatter.summary: Arcane Tradition for the Wizard

entries.body:
The Celestial Summoner explores the cosmic secrets of angels and the laws of the good. As one, you combine your knowledge of arcane mysteries with religious teachings, and learn how to summon celestials to your aid.

Angels and other heavenly creatures answer your call if and only if your alignment is good, your cause is good, or they deem it worthy or necessary to help you.

## Features

> [!info]- Heaven 101 (level 2)
> You have extensive knowledge about celestials, having studied them profusely. Starting at 2nd level, you benefit from the following:
>
> - You can add your proficiency bonus to the Intelligence (Arcana, History, and Religion) checks you make about celestial creatures. If you are already proficient, you add it again.
>
> - You gain advantage on Charisma (Insight, Persuasion) checks against angels.
>
> - You can conjure a guardian angel (p. 250) as a familiar when you cast the find familiar spell.

> [!info]- Celestial Summoning (level 2)
> Starting at 2nd level, you can use your action to summon a celestial with a challenge rating of 1 or lower. This challenge rating increases to 2 at 6th, 4 at 10th, and 6 at 14th level.
>
> The celestial appears in an unoccupied space that you can see within range. You must maintain your concentration on the celestial (as if concentrating on a spell) for it to remain. It disappears when you lose your concentration, it drops to 0 hit points or after 10 minutes.
>
> The celestial is friendly to you and your companions for the duration. Roll initiative for the celestial, which has its own turns. It obeys any verbal commands that you issue it (no action required by you), as long as the celestial is also willing to execute the action. If you don't issue any commands to the celestial, it defends itself against hostile creatures but otherwise takes no actions.
>
> The GM has the celestial's statistics.
>
> Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest to use it again. You can use this feature twice at 6th, three times at 10th, and four times at 14th level.

> [!info]- Exalted Conjuration (level 6)
> At 6th level, you become an expert on the use of magical energies to summon heavenly creatures and you can choose to apply the heavenly creature template (p. 255) to a creature you summon by a conjuration spell.

> [!info]- Celestial Fury (level 10)
> Starting at 10th level, the bond between you and those you summon allows you to channel radiant energy. While concentrating on a spell that summons a celestial or on the Celestial Summoning feature, you can use your bonus action to expend a spell slot. When you do so, choose a number of allies equal to the level of the expended slot that you can see within 60 feet of you. The chosen allies' melee and ranged weapon attacks deal an extra 3 radiant damage for 1 minute.

> [!info]- Celestial Resurrection (level 14)
> Starting at 14th level, when you drop to 0 hit points, you can choose to expend a use of Celestial Summoning feature as a reaction, and drop to 5d8 hit points instead.

_From Corpus Angelus._

entries.title: Education
entries.summary: Arcane Tradition for the Wizard

frontmatter.title: Education
frontmatter.summary: Arcane Tradition for the Wizard

entries.body:
Education is one of the greatest virtues in existence, and you are the carrier of its enlightening flame.

You are a teacher of the arcane arts. You start your academic career from the bottom and make your way up as you improve in the ways of magic and learn how to teach it to others. Your students and their education are more important to you than magic itself. Teaching can sometimes be hard and require restless nights of hard work, but the students appreciate your patience and this gives you a sense of accomplishment.

To start your career, you graduated from a school that teaches the basics of the arcane arts and convinced a professor to let you work for them.

## Features

> [!info]- Instructor (level 2)
> You start to read and grade exams and homework, and report them to your superiors. Through this process, you learn the basics of teaching.
>
> Starting at 2nd level, the money and time others spend to copy a spell from your spellbook are halved.

> [!info]- Supervised Cantrips (level 2)
> Beginning at 2nd level, you can teach how to cast a cantrip to others even if they have no knowledge of the arcane arts.
>
> You give an hour-long lecture to a creature and lend them the ability to cast one cantrip that you know. The creature uses your spellcasting ability to cast the cantrip. You can lend a maximum number of cantrips equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1).
>
> You cannot lend more than one cantrip to a creature using this feature. You can end this effect on any creature that you are sharing a cantrip with at any time.

> [!info]- Master Instructor (level 6)
> At 6th level, you learn how to effectively use your academic skills during a moment of conflict. You can use this feature to benefit from one of the following options of your choice:
>
> **Negative Feedback.** As a bonus action, you give negative feedback to a creature concentrating on a spell. If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier) or its concentration is broken.
>
> **Positive Feedback.** As a reaction, you give positive feedback to a creature casting a spell. If the creature can see or hear you, the creature's spell save DC and spell attack modifier increase by 1 until the start of its next turn.
>
> **Quick Course.** You instruct a creature on how to end an ongoing magical effect on themselves. As an action, choose a creature that can see or hear you and the creature can repeat the saving throw of a spell that is currently affecting it, ending the spell on a success. The creature makes the saving throw with advantage.
>
> You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) and you regain the ability to do so after you finish a short or long rest.

> [!info]- Assistant Professor (level 10)
> Beginning at 10th level, you are an assistant professor. You prepare homework and some exam questions, and you directly report to the professor that you are working under. During this time in your career, you learn to design creative challenges for the improvement of your students through the questions you prepare.
>
> As an action, you ask a question to a creature, who must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw or be stunned for 1 minute. The creature repeats the saving throw at the start of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. The creature must be able to understand you or isn't affected by this feature.

> [!info]- Professor (level 14)
> At 14th level, you become a professor. You prepare the curriculum and have the authority to give a certificate to your graduate students as proof of their efforts and achievements. Upon graduation, a student becomes qualified to choose this arcane tradition.
>
> To become a professor, you learned to tap into the untapped magical energies inside your students. You can cast the spells that have a range of self, with a range of touch instead.

_From Corpus Angelus._

entries.title: Evocation
entries.summary: Arcane Tradition for the Wizard

frontmatter.title: Evocation
frontmatter.summary: Arcane Tradition for the Wizard

entries.body:
_Arcane Tradition (Wizard subclass)_

You focus your study on magic that creates powerful elemental effects such as bitter cold, searing flame, rolling thunder, crackling lightning, and burning acid. Some evokers find employment in military forces, serving as artillery to blast enemy armies from afar. Others use their spectacular power to protect the weak, while some seek their own gain as bandits, adventurers, or aspiring tyrants.

## Features

> [!info]- Evocation Savant (level 2)
> Beginning when you select this school at 2nd level, the gold and time you must spend to copy an evocation spell into your spellbook is halved.

> [!info]- Sculpt Spells (level 2)
> Beginning at 2nd level, you can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocation spells. When you cast an evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 + the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

> [!info]- Potent Cantrip (level 6)
> Starting at 6th level, your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your cantrip, the creature takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

> [!info]- Empowered Evocation (level 10)
> Beginning at 10th level, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of any wizard evocation spell you cast.

> [!info]- Overchannel (level 14)
> Starting at 14th level, you can increase the power of your simpler spells. When you cast a wizard spell of 1st through 5th level that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell.
>
> The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a long rest, you take 2d12 necrotic damage for each level of the spell, immediately after you cast it. Each time you use this feature again before finishing a long rest, the necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12. This damage ignores resistance and immunity.

entries.title: School of Sealing
entries.summary: Arcane Tradition for the Wizard

frontmatter.title: School of Sealing
frontmatter.summary: Arcane Tradition for the Wizard

entries.body:
This school of magic is all about enhancing or reducing the effects of spells by sealing them in a specific way. The wizards of this school usually work with spells from the school of abjuration and aim to provide better protection through magic. Wizards of this school are called sealers and are generally the protectors of the groups they are in.

## Features

> [!info]- Weakening Seal (level 2)
> Starting at 2nd level, you can prevent a creature from using its powers. As a reaction, you can target a creature within 30 feet of you. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be affected by one of the following effects of your choice:
>
> - The target's speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.
>
> - The target has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes within 1 minute.
>
> - The target takes 1d6 radiant damage.
>
> - The target has disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes within 1 minute.
>
> You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses after you finish a long rest.

> [!info]- Ritual of Protecting Seal (level 2)
> Also at 2nd level, you can place a seal on objects to protect them against specific types of creatures. To do so, you perform a 1-hour ritual with the item and choose one of the following creature types; aberration, celestial, dragon, elemental, fey, fiend, giant, monstrosity, ooze, or undead.
>
> If a creature of the chosen type tries to carry the item, it takes 4d6 force damage, and an extra 4d6 force damage at the start of each of its turns while carrying it.
>
> The sealed item retains its new properties for 1 week, for the duration of which it also becomes a magic item.
>
> The seal is visible to the naked eye, and a creature can discern the nature of the seal by means of a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) check.
>
> The force damage increases to 5d6 at 10th, 6d6 at 14th, and 7d6 at 18th level.
>
> In addition, when you reach 14th level, the effects of the ritual become permanent, and you can seal the item against evil-aligned creatures instead of choosing a single creature type. Only you or a wish spell can dispel the effects of the ritual.
>
> Once you use this feature, you must finish a long rest to do so again.

> [!info]- Interruptive Seal (level 6)
> At 6th level, you learn to form a seal between a creature and magic. Whenever you cast the dispel magic or the counterspell spells, you can choose to have advantage on the ability check required by the spell.
>
> In addition, when you cast the banishment spell, the target has disadvantage on the Charisma saving throw, and you only have to keep it under the effect of the spell for 5 turns instead of 1 minute for the target to remain banished.
>
> You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain any expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

> [!info]- Detailed Knowledge of Sealing (level 10)
> At 10th level, your knowledge of protection magic reaches immense heights, allowing you to cast an abjuration spell without expending a spell slot. Once you use this feature in this way, you must finish a long rest to do so again.
>
> In addition, choose one of the following creature types: aberration, celestial, dragon, elemental, fey, fiend, giant, monstrosity, ooze, or undead. When you cast a spell that targets a creature of the chosen type, the target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be stunned until the end of its next turn. You can change the chosen type of creature during a long rest.

> [!info]- Master Sealer (level 14)
> At 14th level, you can close planar gates, teleportation circles, and portals by performing a 1-hour ritual.
>
> You can also choose to close such gates and portals more quickly. As an action, you can expend a spell slot of 6th level or higher and consume spell components worth 500 gold pieces to close a planar gate or portal.
>
> When closed in this way, gates or portals are not destroyed and can be activated again.
>
> This feature does not work on the gates and portals created by gods or other prominent divine forces.

_From Corpus Angelus._

frontmatter.summary: A template for characters with angelic blood; gain it at creation or in

entries.body:
Angelics are people that have angelic blood coursing through their veins, for one reason or another (see below). The blood of angels bestows grace upon its carrier, affecting the carrier's body and soul. Angelics are partial to good and graceful acts, and possess an unearthly charisma.

The angels who share blood with the angelic watch over them; both to guide them through possible dangers and to make sure that angelic blood is put to good use.

## A Heavenly Origin

One can be born an angelic or become one through the processes laid out below.

Occasionally, an angel is so impressed by the actions of a mortal that it rewards the mortal with its blood, transforming the mortal into an angelic creature.

Even more rarely, if a mortal uses an angelic relic, guards a sacred area, or interacts with another heavenly source for long periods of time, the source slowly transforms it into an angelic.

## Double-Edged Sword

Angelics are generally noteworthy characters, and are easily recognized in crowds. Although this can make them valuable allies, it also means that they are more easily noticed by foes.

Aberrations and evil spellcasters hunt them down to use them as unique spell components, and fiends seek their soul to make them suffer or use them against their heavenly enemies.

Also, if an angelic abandons the ways of the angel whose blood runs through their veins, the angel can take the powers of the blood back, or even hunt the angelic if it commits an unforgivable crime.

## Like Angel, Like Blooded

An angelic displays the characteristics of the angel whose blood it shares. For example, if an angelic has the blood of an angel of war, it tends to become an honorable warrior.

## Angelic Template

You can choose this template while creating your character, or you can acquire it in the course of the game at the GM's discretion.

When you become an angelic, you retain all your statistics and gain the following benefits:

**Ability score improvement:** Your Charisma score increases by 1, up to a maximum of 21.

> [!info]- Angelic Body and Soul
> The necrotic damage you take increases by 3, and the radiant damage you take is reduced by 3.
>
> These numbers increase by 2 for every 4 levels you have after 1st.
>
> You also carry a physical mark. This mark can be an angelic sign on your body, jade green eyes, marble-like skin, or anything else you can think of, so long as the GM approves of your choice.

> [!info]- Angelic Existence
> You age more slowly than before. Your lifespan is doubled, and you only require half the ration and half the sleep to sustain yourself: 1-day's worth of rations sustain you for two days, and you can finish a long rest in half the time you did before.

> [!info]- Creature Type
> You retain your old creature type, and become a celestial. Since you can be detected by a detect evil and good spell, or affected by a protection from evil and good spell, the GM should keep in mind that being a celestial may cause serious peril.

> [!info]- Angelic Manifestation
> Your angelic blood manifests itself more strongly as you gain more power.
>
> When you reach 11th level, you choose one of the following benefits:
>
> - Your weapon attacks become magical and deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage on a hit.
>
> - You sprout angelic wings, thus gaining a flying speed of 30 feet.
>
> - You can cast the planar binding spell. Once you use this feature, you must finish a long rest to use it again.

_From Corpus Angelus._

entries.title: Discovery Features
entries.body:
# Discovery & Cross-Linking (Phase 3)

This document explains the discovery features added in Phase 3.

---

## Source Badges

Every entry now displays a **source badge** indicating where the content comes from:

### Badge Types

**SRD 5.1**

- Official D&D 5e material from the System Reference Document
- Licensed under Creative Commons
- Reliable, well-tested rules

**Homebrew**

- Custom content created for your table
- DM-approved house rules or campaign-specific options
- May differ from official rules

**Corpus Angelus**

- Third-party material from external sources
- Community-created or published supplements

### What Badges Look Like

At the top of each entry page, you'll see the source clearly marked with a colored badge:

- SRD 5.1: Blue badge
- Homebrew: Yellow badge
- Corpus Angelus: Brown badge

### Why This Matters

- **Players know what's official** (SRD vs custom)
- **DMs can filter by source** (if needed)
- **Citation is clear** (legal requirements met)
- **No confusion** about which rules apply

---

## Bidirectional Spell/Class Linking

Spells and Classes now link to each other automatically:

### How It Works

**Class Pages Show:**

- All spells available to that class
- Organized by level (Cantrips, 1st-level, etc.)
- Links to full spell pages

**Spell Pages Show:**

- Which classes can learn this spell
- Which subclasses specialize in it (if any)
- Related spells and abilities

### Example: Warlock

Visit the [[Warlock]] page and you'll see:

```
Warlock Spells Available:
- Cantrips: Eldritch Blast, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion, ...
- 1st-level: Armor of Agathys, Hex, Witch Bolt, ...
- 2nd-level: Darkness, Invisibility, Misty Step, ...
```

Click any spell to see its full page, which now shows:

```
Available to: Warlock (primary), Bard (via 6th-level list)
Related Options: Agonizing Blast (invocation), Hex (1st-level)
```

### Why This Matters

- **Players understand their spell options** without searching
- **Easy cross-reference** between classes and spells
- **Discovery of related options** (spells + invocations + features)
- **No separate hunting** for "what spells can my class use?"

---

## Graph View Filtering

The **graph view** (network visualization) now has filtering options.

### Filter Modes

**View All (Default)**

- Shows entire knowledge graph
- 1000+ entries and links
- Can be overwhelming

**Campaign Only**

- Shows only this campaign's entries
- Related classes, spells, items filtered in
- Great for campaign-specific discovery

**Custom Content Only**

- Shows only Homebrew + Corpus Angelus
- Filters out SRD material
- Useful for "what did we customize?"

### How to Use

1. Open graph view (icon on right sidebar)
2. Look for filter toggle (top-right of graph)
3. Select: "View All" | "Campaign Only" | "Custom Only"
4. Graph updates instantly

### Why This Matters

- **Graph view is now useful** (not just a hairball)
- **Campaign-specific discovery** (see what's in your campaign)
- **Content audit** (quickly see your homebrew)
- **Less overwhelm** for new players

---

## Media Organization Strategy

Media files (images) are now organized by type and usage.

### Folder Structure

```
content/media/
├─ characters/        (NPC portraits, character art)
├─ locations/         (Place maps, scene images)
├─ items/             (Item illustrations)
├─ monsters/          (Creature art)
├─ campaigns/         (Campaign-specific images)
│   ├─ ra-golvek/
│   ├─ vyrun/
│   └─ curse-of-strahd/
└─ other/             (Miscellaneous)
```

### Naming Convention

Use descriptive names:

```
Good:    npc_tavern_keeper.jpg, map_city_center.png
Bad:     image_1.jpg, temp.png
```

### Usage

Upload images via Pages CMS:

1. Go to character/spell/item entry
2. Click "Picture (optional)" field
3. Upload from Media area
4. Image displays on entry page

### Benefits

- **Visual entries** (players can see what things look like)
- **Organized** (easy to find and reuse images)
- **Campaign cohesion** (consistent visual style)
- **Future-proof** (media grows, stays organized)

---

## All Discovery Features Together

**Spell Discovery Example:**

1. Open [[Spells]]
2. Click a spell name
3. See: Source badge (SRD | Homebrew), Available classes, Related options
4. Click a class to see what spells it uses
5. Open graph view and filter to "Campaign Only"
6. See how spells connect in your campaign

**Result:** Integrated, interconnected knowledge base

---

## Testing the Features

### Source Badges

- [ ] Visit any entry (spell, item, class)
- [ ] Verify source badge visible at top
- [ ] Check color matches type (blue=SRD, yellow=Homebrew, brown=Corpus)

### Spell/Class Linking

- [ ] Visit [[Warlock]] class page
- [ ] Scroll to spells section
- [ ] Verify spells listed and clickable
- [ ] Click a spell
- [ ] Verify spell page shows Warlock as available class

### Graph View Filtering

- [ ] Open graph view (icon on right sidebar)
- [ ] Look for filter toggle
- [ ] Switch between "View All" / "Campaign Only"
- [ ] Graph updates

### Media Organization

- [ ] Check Pages CMS → (any entry with image field)
- [ ] Verify Media folder is organized
- [ ] Upload a test image
- [ ] Verify it displays on entry page

---

## Integration with Previous Phases

**Phase 1 (Foundation):**

- Metadata infrastructure ready
- Source field standardized

**Phase 2 (Onboarding):**

- New players know where to start
- Campaign hubs guide exploration

**Phase 3 (Discovery):**

- Badges help identify content type
- Linking enables cross-discovery
- Graph view supports exploration
- Media brings entries to life

**Result:** Complete, cohesive user experience

---

## Next: Full Build & Test

Build your site and test all features. If everything works, you're done!

```bash
npm run docs
```

Then:

1. Test each feature above
2. Get feedback from a new player
3. Deploy when confident

---

entries.title: Getting Started
entries.body:
# Getting Started: Campaign Archive Guide

Welcome to the Campaign Archive! This page explains what you can find here and how to use it.

---

## What Is This Site?

This is a **D&D 5e wiki** for player-facing campaign information. It includes:

- **Campaign content:** Sessions, NPCs, locations, loot
- **Character building:** Classes, spells, items, feats
- **Rules references:** House rules, mechanic clarifications
- **SRD material:** Official D&D 5e rules (used under license)

---

## Three Ways to Use This Site

### 1. Building a Character (First Time?)

**[[character-builder|Read the character building guide]]** for a step-by-step walkthrough.

**Quick summary:**

1. Pick a [[character-options/races|race]]
2. Pick a [[character-options/classes|class]]
3. (Optional) Pick a [[character-options/subclasses|subclass]]
4. (Optional) Pick [[character-options/feats|feats]]
5. You're ready to play!

---

### 2. Playing in a Campaign (Ongoing)

**Click your campaign name:**

- **[[campaigns/ra-golvek|Ra Gol'vek]]**
- **[[Vyrun]]**
- **[[Curse of Strahd]]**

Or visit the [[Campaigns|campaign directory]] to choose a campaign.

Each campaign has:

- **Sessions:** What happened and when
- **NPCs:** Characters you interact with
- **Locations:** Places you've visited
- **Loot:** Items you've found

---

### 3. Referencing Rules During Play

**Need something fast?**

- **Spell?** → [[Spells]]
- **Monster stats?** → [[Monsters]]
- **Item effects?** → [[Items]]
- **Rule clarification?** → [[Rules]]

---

## Navigation Tips

### Search (Top Left)

Type to search for anything: spells, items, NPCs, rules.

### Explorer (Left Sidebar)

Browse the file structure. Useful for discovering categories.

### Links

Click `[[like this]]` to jump to related content. Many pages link to each other, so you can explore from any starting point.

### Campaign Pages

Each campaign has **tabs** (Sessions, Characters, Locations, All entries). Use tabs to filter what you're looking for.

---

## For New Players

**Step 1:** [[character-builder|Read "How to Build a Character"]]

**Step 2:** Pick your campaign ([[campaigns/ra-golvek|Ra Gol'vek]], [[Vyrun]], or [[Curse of Strahd]])

**Step 3:** Read the campaign overview to understand the setting

**Step 4:** Check the Sessions tab to see what's happened so far

**Step 5:** At the table, use this site to look up spells, items, and rules

---

## For Returning Players

**Before session:**

- Check your campaign page for session notes
- Review NPCs you'll encounter
- Brush up on spells/items you'll use

**During session:**

- Look up spell effects and ranges
- Check monster stats
- Reference house rules

**After session:**

- Ask your DM to add session notes
- Update your character if it changed

---

## For Dungeon Masters

**Setting up a campaign:**

1. Go to your campaign page
2. Add an overview (what's this campaign about?)
3. Use Pages CMS to add sessions, NPCs, locations

**During prep:**

- Add session summaries before play
- Link NPCs to sessions
- Track campaign-specific loot

**House rules:**

- Add to [[Rules]] section
- Link from relevant classes/spells
- Share with players before game

---

## How Content Is Organized

### SRD vs Custom

- **SRD 5.1** = Official D&D material (from System Reference Document)
- **Homebrew** = Custom content for your table
- **Corpus Angelus** = External third-party material

Look for the **Source** badge on each page to see what's official vs custom.

### Complete vs Incomplete

- **Complete** = Full information, ready to use
- **Incomplete** = Stub entry, being filled in

Incomplete entries won't show up in new-player search. Ask your DM for details.

### Campaign-Specific Content

Each campaign can have:

- Custom house rules
- Session-specific NPCs
- Custom items or monsters
- Campaign-unique lore

---

## Getting Help

### "I don't know where to start"

→ [[character-builder|Read the character building guide]]

### "What's in this campaign?"

→ Click your campaign name and read the overview

### "Where do I find [something]?"

→ Use the search bar (top left)

### "What does [rule] mean?"

→ Check [[Rules]] or ask your DM

### "I found an error or missing info"

→ Tell your DM, or ask them to update the page

---

## Quick Links

- **[[Character Builder|How to build a character]]** — Guided walkthrough
- **[[character-builder|Full character building guide]]** — Detailed reference
- **[[character-options/classes|Classes]]** — Your role in the party
- **[[Spells]]** — Magic reference
- **[[Items]]** — Equipment and treasure
- **[[Monsters]]** — Enemy reference
- **[[Rules]]** — House rules and clarifications
- **[[Campaigns]]** — Browse campaign hubs
- **[[campaigns/ra-golvek|Ra Gol'vek]]** — Campaign 1
- **[[Vyrun]]** — Campaign 2
- **[[Curse of Strahd]]** — Campaign 3

---

## One More Thing

**This site is for you.** If something is confusing, ask your DM to clarify or improve it. The archive is a living document—it gets better as players use it.

Have fun!

---

entries.body:
_Weapon (arrow), very rare_

An arrow of slaying is a magic weapon meant to slay a particular kind of creature. Some are more focused than others; for example, there are both arrows of dragon slaying and arrows of blue dragon slaying. If a creature belonging to the type, race, or group associated with an arrow of slaying takes damage from the arrow, the creature must make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw, taking an extra 6d10 piercing damage on a failed save, or half as much extra damage on a successful one.

Once an arrow of slaying deals its extra damage to a creature, it becomes a nonmagical arrow.

Other types of magic ammunition of this kind exist, such as bolts of slaying meant for a crossbow, though arrows are most common.

---

**Rarity:** Very Rare

_Armor (plate), rare (requires attunement)_

While wearing this armor, you have resistance to one of the following damage types: bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing. The GM chooses the type or determines it randomly.

_**Curse.**_ This armor is cursed, a fact that is revealed only when an identify spell is cast on the armor or you attune to it. Attuning to the armor curses you until you are targeted by the remove curse spell or similar magic; removing the armor fails to end the curse. entries.body:
_Armor (scale mail), very rare (requires attunement)_

Dragon scale mail is made of the scales of a black dragon. Sometimes dragons collect their cast-off scales and gift them to humanoids. Other times, hunters carefully skin and preserve the hide of a dead dragon. In either case, dragon scale mail is highly valued.

While wearing this armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC, you have advantage on saving throws against the Frightful Presence and breath weapons of dragons, and you have resistance to acid damage.

Additionally, you can focus your senses as an action to magically discern the distance and direction to the closest black dragon within 30 miles of you. This special action can't be used again until the next dawn.

entries.body:
_Armor (scale mail), very rare (requires attunement)_

Dragon scale mail is made of the scales of one kind of dragon. Sometimes dragons collect their cast-off scales and gift them to humanoids. Other times, hunters carefully skin and preserve the hide of a dead dragon. In either case, dragon scale mail is highly valued.

While wearing this armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC, you have advantage on saving throws against the Frightful Presence and breath weapons of dragons, and you have resistance to one damage type that is determined by the kind of dragon that provided the scales (see the table).

Additionally, you can focus your senses as an action to magically discern the distance and direction to the closest dragon within 30 miles of you that is of the same type as the armor. This special action can't be used again until the next dawn.

| Dragon | Resistance |
| ------ | ---------- |
| Black  | Acid       |
| Blue   | Lightning  |
| Brass  | Fire       |
| Bronze | Lightning  |
| Copper | Acid       |
| Gold   | Fire       |
| Green  | Poison     |
| Red    | Fire       |
| Silver | Cold       |
| White  | Cold       |

entries.body:
_Potion, uncommon_

This concoction looks, smells, and tastes like a potion of healing or other beneficial potion. However, it is actually poison masked by illusion magic. An identify spell reveals its true nature.

If you drink it, you take 3d6 poison damage, and you must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned. At the start of each of your turns while you are poisoned in this way, you take 3d6 poison damage. At the end of each of your turns, you can repeat the saving throw. On a successful save, the poison damage you take on your subsequent turns decreases by 1d6. The poison ends when the damage decreases to 0.

entries.summary: Ring, legendary (requires attunement)

frontmatter.title: Ring of Air Elemental Command
frontmatter.summary: Ring, legendary (requires attunement)

entries.body:
_Ring, legendary (requires attunement)_

This ring is linked to the Elemental Plane of Air.

While wearing this ring, you have advantage on attack rolls against air elementals, and they have disadvantage on attack rolls against you. In addition, you have access to properties based on the Elemental Plane of Air.

The ring has 5 charges. It regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. Spells cast from the ring have a save DC of 17.

You can expend 2 of the ring's charges to cast dominate monster on an air elemental. In addition, when you fall, you descend 60 feet per round and take no damage from falling. You can also speak and understand Auran.

If you help slay an air elemental while attuned to the ring, you gain access to the following additional properties:

You have resistance to lightning damage.

You have a flying speed equal to your walking speed and can hover.

You can cast the following spells from the ring, expending the necessary number of charges: chain lightning (3 charges), gust of wind (2 charges), or wind wall (1 charge).
